t: This classic malt has a nose of marmalade on hot buttered toast, dabs of honey, sea breezes over sand dunes, grapefruit peel, eucalyptus, dark
f: This classic malt has a nose of marmalade on hot buttered toast, dabs of honey, sea breezes over sand dunes, grapefruit peel, eucalyptus, dark chocolate, and seasoned oak. Rich and full-bodied with tangy citrus peels, honey, marmalade, lots of salinity, candied citrus, almonds, and malt. A dry finish of salt, citrus peel, and traces of honey.

t: Not to be overlooked, this classic dram has a nose of honey, banana chip, malted barley, Cheerios, vanilla ice cream, and toasted spices, with light
f: Not to be overlooked, this classic dram has a nose of honey, banana chip, malted barley, Cheerios, vanilla ice cream, and toasted spices, with light smoke weaving between the bourbon cask flavors. Sweet-tasting heather honey, baked green apple, vanilla sponge, and pear; the flavors evolve, layering on caramel, cinnamon frosting, baked pastries, nutmeg, and black pepper. The finish is fruity, with pear, vanilla, and cinnamon.

n: The ImpEx Collection 14 year old 2011 Vintage Burnside Chateau Latour Barrique (No. 24789), 63.8%
t: Finishing scotch in a wine barrel isn’t a novel concept, but doing so in a cask that once held a first-growth Bordeaux takes the idea to a
f: Finishing scotch in a wine barrel isn’t a novel concept, but doing so in a cask that once held a first-growth Bordeaux takes the idea to a different level. This has an extremely dark color that’s reminiscent of cola, with an earthy nose that also has guava, kiwi, and other tropical fruits. The first sip rewards you with sweetness—toasted pralines and baked apples call you in—followed by chocolate that lasts through the finish.

n: Kentucky Peerless 10 year old Henry Kraver Old Reserve, 58.5%
t: The first age-stated bourbon from Peerless is a bold one, chock-full of dark and robust flavors. Aromas of raisin, vanilla bean, baking spice, orange
f: The first age-stated bourbon from Peerless is a bold one, chock-full of dark and robust flavors. Aromas of raisin, vanilla bean, baking spice, orange peel, bread pudding, and caramel syrup emerge from the glass. The velvety palate ramps up the barrel char and adds tobacco, softened by more vanilla and baking spice sweetness. The finish is lengthy and brings the focus back to the barrel—wood spice and char reign supreme

t: For this inaugural Blueprint bourbon, Blue Run combined two mashbills, one wheated, the other comprised of 80% corn, 15% rye, and 5% malted barley.
f: For this inaugural Blueprint bourbon, Blue Run combined two mashbills, one wheated, the other comprised of 80% corn, 15% rye, and 5% malted barley. The nose is a touch reticent and slightly musty, yielding Ovaltine, sugar cookie, simple syrup, and chocolate-covered strawberries. Much more chocolate arrives on the palate, though there’s also a pop of black pepper, pound cake, and red fruit. Chocolate crinkle cookies and berry fruit combine for an alluring finish.

n: Kilchoman 18 year old Family Collection Bourbon Cask, 50%
t: The nose is incredibly soft, with apple pie filling, grilled pineapple, vanilla cream, peach, heather honey, fading peat smoke, oak shavings, and a
f: The nose is incredibly soft, with apple pie filling, grilled pineapple, vanilla cream, peach, heather honey, fading peat smoke, oak shavings, and a hint of cinnamon breakfast cereal. Quietly elegant, with flavors of Seville orange peel, baked pastries, and a spritz of sea spray followed by apricot jam, walnut, and malted milk. A long-lingering finish of baked fruit, lemon peel, and salt crystals follows.

n: Barrell 12 year old French Oak Cask Finished Blend, 56.7%
t: A blend of bourbons sourced from Kentucky, Indiana, Tennessee, and Wyoming, all aged 12 to 15 years, this whiskey’s French oak finish is the
f: A blend of bourbons sourced from Kentucky, Indiana, Tennessee, and Wyoming, all aged 12 to 15 years, this whiskey’s French oak finish is the star of the show. Heady baking spice, vanilla, strawberry jam, clove, and caramel pull you into the glass. Despite being higher proof, the palate is silky smooth, draped with spice, vanilla icing, cooked cherries, toasted marshmallow, and Heath bar. More of the same on the finish, as gooey toasted marsh- mallow melds with vanilla, barrel char, and a hint of black pepper.

n: Virginia Distilling Co. The Split Barrel Project American (Project 1), 45%
t: A 50/50 blend of VDC’s single malt and Green River bourbon. The nose leads with dried apricot, orange peel, cinnamon applesauce, Triscuits,
f: A 50/50 blend of VDC’s single malt and Green River bourbon. The nose leads with dried apricot, orange peel, cinnamon applesauce, Triscuits, Frosted Flakes, and French vanilla. Fruits keep coming on the palate, like baked apples, poached pears, and baking spice. The bourbon reveals itself on the finish, adding vanilla custard and oak amid familiar orchard fruits and plum. An interesting blending showcase, but it’d be even better with deeper integration.

n: Gambit No. 6 6 year old Wine, Apple Brandy, Sherry, and Tokaji Cask Finished, 48%
t: This is unusual given its finishing in six different casks: chardonnay, cabernet sauvi- gnon, apple brandy, muscatel, oloroso sherry, and tokaji.
f: This is unusual given its finishing in six different casks: chardonnay, cabernet sauvi- gnon, apple brandy, muscatel, oloroso sherry, and tokaji. Aromas of baked peach, pecan pie, cherry turnovers, and mixed berries rise up to meet you. The palate is grippy and big to start, with some herbs and tannins. Water brings on quite a change, adding tea, toasted corn, and black peppercorn spice before a somewhat dry finish. An earthy pour.

t: Aromas of warm baking spice, plentiful vanilla, pancakes, butter, and maple syrup fill the nose. Loads of breakfast and bakery flavors are accented
f: Aromas of warm baking spice, plentiful vanilla, pancakes, butter, and maple syrup fill the nose. Loads of breakfast and bakery flavors are accented by pepper spice, raspberry jam, chocolate, and vanilla. The long, smooth finish serves up more vanilla and spice. Despite the proof, it’s so delicate, flavorful, smooth, and delicious.

t: Even at its slightly elevated proof, this is easy drinking with enough depth to make it a daily sipper. Aromas of honeyed grains, cola, and toffee
f: Even at its slightly elevated proof, this is easy drinking with enough depth to make it a daily sipper. Aromas of honeyed grains, cola, and toffee rise from the glass, backed by peach iced tea and vanilla frosting. The palate is nutty, with peanuts and candied pecans mingling with brown sugar, caramel, and cornbread. With water, fresh peaches and a hint of strawberries emerge. The finish balances coffee bitterness and honey sweetness.

n: WhistlePig 10 year old Rye, White, and Blue Piggybank, 55%
t: Created to commemorate the 250th anniversary of the U.S. (and priced accordingly), this straight rye comes in a piggy bank-shaped bottle that’s
f: Created to commemorate the 250th anniversary of the U.S. (and priced accordingly), this straight rye comes in a piggy bank-shaped bottle that’s hard to ignore. It has a sweet, boozy nose that includes vanilla pudding, maple syrup, toasted coconut, and fudge-covered berries. On the palate, crème brûlée and molasses are augmented by savory mixed nuts and a wisp of mint. It grows more minty with water, which also brings chocolate.

t: Distilled in 2017, this single cask has a heady nose of glacé cherry, ginger root, dried vine fruit, blueberry muffin, butter toffee,
f: Distilled in 2017, this single cask has a heady nose of glacé cherry, ginger root, dried vine fruit, blueberry muffin, butter toffee, marmalade peel, and festive spices. Orange marmalade on the taste buds, with the spices ramping up to a lengthy peppery buzz, layering on gingerbread and ripe fleshy plum; a splash of water delivers a sweeter profile of sugar-coated plums without altering the thick, mouthcoating finish.

n: Rebel Kyle Busch Single Barrel Select (No. 86213), 54%
t: Picked by recently departed NASCAR legend Kyle Busch, this has notes of ginger ale, key lime pie, vanilla frosting, and baked berries. It has an
f: Picked by recently departed NASCAR legend Kyle Busch, this has notes of ginger ale, key lime pie, vanilla frosting, and baked berries. It has an interesting palate of powdered sugar, toffee, shortbread cookies, and burnt sugar. The finish adds caramel, cream soda, and, at the very end, hints of dark chocolate. The palate bites occasionally, but a few drops of water go a long way in taming it.

t: This blend of bourbons aged between 8 and 15 years was distilled in Kentucky, Indiana, Tennessee, and Maryland. The nose balances youth and
f: This blend of bourbons aged between 8 and 15 years was distilled in Kentucky, Indiana, Tennessee, and Maryland. The nose balances youth and maturity, with bright fruits tempered by dusty leather and well-worn oak. The palate opens with sweetened cereal grains and a hint of marshmallow. Water draws out apricot and apples. With time, it turns more savory with chicory, walnuts, and dried herbs. The finish is exceptionally long with seasoned oak and more leather.

n: Copper & Cask 11 year old Small Batch Series (Batch 16), 58.1%,
t: This high-rye bourbon is sourced from an undisclosed Indiana distillery. It’s a spice bomb, with loads of cinnamon, nutmeg, and allspice on the
f: This high-rye bourbon is sourced from an undisclosed Indiana distillery. It’s a spice bomb, with loads of cinnamon, nutmeg, and allspice on the nose, as well as toasted almonds and vanilla ice cream. On the palate, more classic bourbon notes emerge, among them powdered sugar, raspberry jam, and even more baking spice, keeping a good thing going. All in all, this is a divine sipper that’s balanced and maintains mouthwatering flavors throughout.

n: Tormore 10 year old Blueprint Cream Sherry Cask, 48%
t: Part of a trio of reworkings of the Tormore core range (hence the name Blueprint) under new owner Elixir Distillers, which acquired the distillery
f: Part of a trio of reworkings of the Tormore core range (hence the name Blueprint) under new owner Elixir Distillers, which acquired the distillery from Pernod Ricard in 2022. This decadent single malt spent 10 years in cream sherry casks, and it shows. The nose is rife with vanilla custard, baking spice, cinnamon sugar, molasses, and gingersnaps. There’s spectacular spice on the palate, along with milk chocolate and red fruit. The finish is rich and punchy, and has more fruit and warming chocolate.

t: Distilled and matured at Great Northern Distillery, Two Stacks blends 50% triple distilled oloroso sherry cask-matured single malt with 40% double
f: Distilled and matured at Great Northern Distillery, Two Stacks blends 50% triple distilled oloroso sherry cask-matured single malt with 40% double distilled single malt and 10% peated single malt matured in bourbon barrels. Nectarine, smoke, white grape, pear, and lemon curd aromas also carry hints of grassiness, eucalyptus, and Band-Aids. Full-flavored, with mango chunks, mandarin, canned peaches, fruit candies, peppercorn, and porridge oats, with a mouth-coating, juicy finish.

n: Two Stacks Triple Sherry Cask Finish, 43%
t: Initially matured in bourbon barrels, then parceled and individually finished in oloroso, amontillado, and PX sherry casks, this has a gorgeous nose
f: Initially matured in bourbon barrels, then parceled and individually finished in oloroso, amontillado, and PX sherry casks, this has a gorgeous nose of orange fondant, apple, feisty pot still spices, and blackberry. It’s fat and oily in the mouth, with melted honey, caramelized apple, pepper, clove, toffee, vanilla, pie crust, and black cherry. The finish is long and spicy, with toasted oak. A superb example of what single pot still can offer.

n: Bardstown Bourbon Company Discovery Series No. 13 Double Barreled American and Hungarian Oak Finished Blend of Straights, 55.4%
t: An alluring nose pulls you in with scents of spice, strawberries and cream, peanut butter and jelly, and Fig Newton. It’s a tad hot on the
f: An alluring nose pulls you in with scents of spice, strawberries and cream, peanut butter and jelly, and Fig Newton. It’s a tad hot on the palate, but there’s plenty to enjoy: More succulent berry fruit emerges alongside vanilla bean panna cotta, caramel syrup, baking spice, and coffee creamer. The finish brings caramel flan, concha pastry, crème brûlée, and milk chocolate.

n: Shortbarrel The Afterswarm Meadowfoam Double Barrel Toasted Honey Cask Finished, 54.3%
t: The nose calls to mind a fall county fair, bringing brown sugar, caramel-dipped apples, freshly baked apple pie, cherry, and cinnamon. Spices take
f: The nose calls to mind a fall county fair, bringing brown sugar, caramel-dipped apples, freshly baked apple pie, cherry, and cinnamon. Spices take the wheel on the palate, offering cinnamon stick, allspice, ground nutmeg, pickled ginger, and hot pepper, all underscored by a pleasant honey-maple sweetness. Chocolate-covered chiles lead the finish, joined by more honey, cinnamon, and very subtle flowers. Despite its nearly year-long finish, it’s very well-balanced throughout.

t: Distilled in Lancaster County from a mashbill of 60% rye, 30% corn, and 10% malted barley, this has a mellow and approachable nose of caramel apple,
f: Distilled in Lancaster County from a mashbill of 60% rye, 30% corn, and 10% malted barley, this has a mellow and approachable nose of caramel apple, cinnamon, assorted baking spices, candy corn, and mint sprigs. The palate has Mexican hot chocolate, chocolate-covered chiles, toffee, and tart sour cherries. The finish evolves some of those flavors into caramel, stroopwafel, white pepper, and mocha.

t: A blend of 50% single grain, 20% single pot still, and 10% single malt matured in bourbon barrels, with 10% single pot still and 10% single malt
f: A blend of 50% single grain, 20% single pot still, and 10% single malt matured in bourbon barrels, with 10% single pot still and 10% single malt matured in PX and oloroso sherry-seasoned casks. Sweet grain and floral aromas, with Honey Nut Cheerios, vanilla ice cream, toasted peppercorn, and wood shavings. Mild on the palate, with honey, vanilla, Frosted Flakes, orange zest, caramel, dried apple, and clove leading into a spicy finish.

n: Buzzard’s Roost Ambuzzador’s Select Single Barrel (June 2025 Release; Barrel 23-76494), 57.5%
t: An annual release picked by members of the brand’s Ambuzzador fan club. It offers cloves in droves on the nose, along with ginger ale and
f: An annual release picked by members of the brand’s Ambuzzador fan club. It offers cloves in droves on the nose, along with ginger ale and candied jalapeños. Ground spices like cinnamon, nutmeg, and cumin lead the palate, followed by mustard seed and dark red berries. The explosive finish adds root beer, pickled ginger, vanilla, and brown sugar. It’s certainly a spice bomb, but one that has impressive depth and complexity.

t: Sourced grain and double-distilled single malt whiskeys matured in bourbon barrels, then finished in oloroso sherry and peated casks. Aromas take
f: Sourced grain and double-distilled single malt whiskeys matured in bourbon barrels, then finished in oloroso sherry and peated casks. Aromas take time to open up: lemon frosting, allspice, peat smoke, cookie dough, chocolate chip, new leather, raisins steeped in vanilla extract, and dunnage earthiness. Excellent flavor balance with heather honey, glazed fruit, dried apricot, smoke, clove, marmalade, and more allspice, then a finish of cinnamon cookies and cacao.

n: Dalmore Select Edition 15 year old (Distilled 2010, Bottled 2025), 49.1%
t: Released in March as a pair alongside a 2007-distilled expression. It was matured mainly in bourbon barrels, along with some apostoles and amoroso
f: Released in March as a pair alongside a 2007-distilled expression. It was matured mainly in bourbon barrels, along with some apostoles and amoroso sherry casks sourced from Gonzalez Byass. Pine, mint tea, earthiness, candle wax, a hint of rancio, and fragrant aged oak on the nose. On the palate, peach tart, baked berries, and light spice. A long finish of chocolate and musty oak. Smoothly textured, beautifully aged, and syrupy but balanced.

t: Skellig matured, finished, and blended this combination of triple-distilled single pot still whiskeys matured in bourbon, PX sherry, and peated
f: Skellig matured, finished, and blended this combination of triple-distilled single pot still whiskeys matured in bourbon, PX sherry, and peated casks. Clouds of baking spices mingle with aromas of light peat, vanilla, berry fruit coulis, leather, and candy cola bottles. It brings warm spiced fruitcake, cola, clove, and gentle smoke to the palate, before a chewy finish of raisins, black licorice, leather, and black pepper.

n: Three Chord RIOT Double Bonded Bottled in Bond Blend, 50%
t: A blend of two bonded ryes from MGP and Bardstown, aged from 4–7 years. It’s fairly sweet on the nose, with cinnamon sugar, Cinnabon
f: A blend of two bonded ryes from MGP and Bardstown, aged from 4–7 years. It’s fairly sweet on the nose, with cinnamon sugar, Cinnabon rolls, coffee cake, and brownies. Spiced chocolate, ground cinnamon, powdered sugar doughnuts, nutmeg, and other baking spices form a well-structured palate with a pleasant oily texture. Those spices return on the finish, a bit sharper than before, now joined by vanilla.

n: King of Kentucky 12 year old Small Batch (Batch 2), 53.75%
t: Tobacco, vanilla, almond paste, marzipan, and aged oak on the nose. Spicy on the palate, with more tobacco and aged oak, plus cinnamon, raspberry
f: Tobacco, vanilla, almond paste, marzipan, and aged oak on the nose. Spicy on the palate, with more tobacco and aged oak, plus cinnamon, raspberry jam, cherry pie, and candied black cherry slightly outpacing chocolate sweetness. There’s more fruit on the finish, mainly luscious red berries. Overall, it’s quite a bit more fruit-forward than the other two in the trio, but it’s a nicely aged and integrated whiskey.

n: New Riff 6 year old Sherry Finished Barrel Proof, 55.95%
t: A rare cask-finished whiskey in the New Riff portfolio, this 100% malted rye is brooding on the nose, with restrained dark fruit, a hint of sherry
f: A rare cask-finished whiskey in the New Riff portfolio, this 100% malted rye is brooding on the nose, with restrained dark fruit, a hint of sherry cask funk, and a whisper of peppery spice. The palate is more welcoming, with raisins, dried cranberries, and cooked apple backed by mint tea, overripe berries, and muted baking spices. The finish is long, with roasted grain, dried spices, and pepper.

t: Created by master blender par excellence Nancy Fraley, who employed the French “petits eaux” dilution method used in cognac making. The
f: Created by master blender par excellence Nancy Fraley, who employed the French “petits eaux” dilution method used in cognac making. The nose is resplendent with cigar ash and tobacco leaf, dried strawberries, vanilla, and mellow herbs. The palate features cherry, anise, red berries, vanilla cream, more tobacco leaf, and pepper spice, with a finish of similar flavors. Not super dynamic, but a very worthy accompaniment to a good cigar.

n: Hard Truth Barrel Finish Reserve Mizunara Oak Finished, 62.3%
t: This straight rye (94% rye, 6% malted barley) is exceptionally dark in the glass, with a cherry cola nose. Cherries abound, hinting at maraschino
f: This straight rye (94% rye, 6% malted barley) is exceptionally dark in the glass, with a cherry cola nose. Cherries abound, hinting at maraschino liqueur, and the copious sweetness is buttressed by a touch of menthol. Water brings out even more flavor, and the finish is delightfully long. Limited release, with 21 barrels made.

n: Remus Gatsby Reserve 15 year old Cask Strength (2025 Edition), 51.4%
t: Made at Ross & Squibb Distillery in Indiana, this ultra-aged bourbon offers a very aromatic nose of cocktail cherries, butterscotch,
f: Made at Ross & Squibb Distillery in Indiana, this ultra-aged bourbon offers a very aromatic nose of cocktail cherries, butterscotch, Werther’s Original, and malted chocolate milkshake. The palate has oak, more cherry, chocolate, bruised apple, and berry-flavored cough syrup. The finish adds leather, with the chocolate growing darker and more bitter.

n: Castle & Key Small Batch 6 year old, 50.5%
t: This fruity, frisky bourbon, now a part of Castle & Key’s permanent lineup, kicks off with dried pineapple, candied orange, vanilla bean,
f: This fruity, frisky bourbon, now a part of Castle & Key’s permanent lineup, kicks off with dried pineapple, candied orange, vanilla bean, Creamsicle, and a trace of lilies on the nose. There’s some wood up front on the palate, but notes of single-origin coffee, açai, and cassis soon smooth it out. The finish turns darker, as dark-roast coffee, semi-sweet chocolate chips, Heath bar, and lemon peel take over.

t: Briny and leathery on the nose, this single malt from Ian Macleod Distillers starts oceanic and austere before giving way to a more balanced, sweeter
f: Briny and leathery on the nose, this single malt from Ian Macleod Distillers starts oceanic and austere before giving way to a more balanced, sweeter sip. While the nose leans into the whisky’s Islay roots, the palate balances peat, iodine, and salt air with lush sweets like caramel candies, flan, and fruit tart. With a dash of water, lemon zest and tart apples are revealed. The finish is light and harmonious with peat and vanilla.

n: Still Austin 6 year old Bottled in Bond Blue Corn (Winter 2025), 50%
t: Made with 26% blue corn in the mashbill. A touch of maple syrup on the nose hints at the parade of sweet flavors that arrives after a sip. Rich
f: Made with 26% blue corn in the mashbill. A touch of maple syrup on the nose hints at the parade of sweet flavors that arrives after a sip. Rich butterscotch combines with tea and hearty wood flavors, and the finish is long and deeply sweet, smacking of butterscotch pudding and a touch of toffee.

t: This one was made from Rosalina, Sebastian, and Barke barley varieties and matured in Pedro Ximénez sherry casks. Raisins, baked plum,
f: This one was made from Rosalina, Sebastian, and Barke barley varieties and matured in Pedro Ximénez sherry casks. Raisins, baked plum, marmalade, and polished leather aromas, with hints of peppercorn and cocoa powder on cappuccino foam. More marmalade, along with lime peel, black pepper, blackberry, leather, and hints of grapefruit on the palate. The spices subside on the finish with Red Vines and dried vine fruits.

t: A combination of two blended components, matured in bourbon and married in oloroso sherry casks respectively, the nose lifts off with flowers, honey,
f: A combination of two blended components, matured in bourbon and married in oloroso sherry casks respectively, the nose lifts off with flowers, honey, white pepper, fresh oak, vanilla cupcakes, lemon shortbread, almond ice cream, and lemon meringue pie. Moreish and distinctive, the flavors take flight through honey, elderflower, lemon, peppercorn, apple pie, caramel, toasted hazelnuts, clove, and banoffee, landing with a flutter of roasted spice and crème brûlée on the finish.

n: Kilchoman 14 year old 20th Anniversary Cask Series 100% Islay Ex-Sherry Butt Matured, 55%
t: In celebration of its 20th anniversary, Islay’s Kilchoman Distillery released four distinct single malts, each one a blend of five casks. On
f: In celebration of its 20th anniversary, Islay’s Kilchoman Distillery released four distinct single malts, each one a blend of five casks. On the nose, this one has notes of brown sugar, graham cracker, and dried fruit, with that classic Islay smoke enticingly entwined. The ashy palate calls to mind campfire coals and tobacco smoke, but there’s delicious dark chocolate and more dark dried fruit. The finish is lengthy and bursting with spice, meatloaf glaze, and, of course, that delicate sweet peat.

t: Finished in American oak casks toasted with volcanic rocks, the nose swirls with pepper, peat smoke, creamy vanilla, cacao, briny oyster shell, and
f: Finished in American oak casks toasted with volcanic rocks, the nose swirls with pepper, peat smoke, creamy vanilla, cacao, briny oyster shell, and windblown driftwood. Sweet, salty, and luxuriously creamy on the palate, with a wave of black pepper, clove, and a hint of root vegetables, before milk chocolate and butterscotch glide into a long, creamy finish. Water amplifies the peat notes and pepperi- ness, and adds red apple flavors.

t: A new permanent fixture in the Eagle Rare lineup. Honey, clove, and whipped cream, anchored by earthy oak on a very aromatic nose. This has a velvety
f: A new permanent fixture in the Eagle Rare lineup. Honey, clove, and whipped cream, anchored by earthy oak on a very aromatic nose. This has a velvety smooth and soft texture; a deliciously gooey palate of honeyed almonds, buttered French toast, raspberry jam, and a bite of pepper spice. Long and delicious on the finish of vanilla ice cream drizzled with honey. Good body, full-flavored, and delicious.

n: Nikka From The Barrel Extra Marriage 40th Anniversary Limited Edition, 51.4%
t: Given an extra 3-month marrying period in oak at Nikka’s Tochigi Aging Cellar, this is gorgeous liquid with rich aromas of caramel, smoke,
f: Given an extra 3-month marrying period in oak at Nikka’s Tochigi Aging Cellar, this is gorgeous liquid with rich aromas of caramel, smoke, honeycomb, Reese’s peanut butter cups, lemongrass, fresh ginger, and a hint of peat bog. Baked citrus, toffee, zesty lemon, and honey flavors, it has more pungent peat smoke than the malt component, rounding out with malt, butterscotch, cocoa powder, and caramel popcorn.

t: A study in tropical fruit, this unconventional Clynelish captures an experimental “pineapple cut” early in distillation, and protects
f: A study in tropical fruit, this unconventional Clynelish captures an experimental “pineapple cut” early in distillation, and protects those flavors through refill cask maturation. Cantaloupe, lychee, ripe pears in sweetened syrup, and the nostalgic aromas of Edinburgh rock and royal icing. With a subtle waxy texture, it’s medium-bodied, offering mango sorbet, pineapple, papaya, and citrus-bright taffy candy, followed by a spiced tropical fruit finish. Come sip the sunshine.

t: Bright and attractive with a nose of lemon-frosted cupcakes, apple blossom, vanilla, and a hint of marmalade, plus sherbet, gooseberry, and Love
f: Bright and attractive with a nose of lemon-frosted cupcakes, apple blossom, vanilla, and a hint of marmalade, plus sherbet, gooseberry, and Love Hearts candy. Light bodied and juicy in the mouth, with fresh raspberries, cream, zesty lime, green apple, and pepper, moving on to ripe fig, aniseed balls, Refreshers, lemon throat lozenges, and orange soda. A refreshing and zesty finish with lemon and gentle spices.

n: The Singleton of Glen Ord Into The Blue 17 year old, 56.2%
t: A fusion of mezcal and sherry influences, this Glen Ord brims with intrigue. The nose reveals papaya, cantaloupe, pear, smoked agave, toasted cedar,
f: A fusion of mezcal and sherry influences, this Glen Ord brims with intrigue. The nose reveals papaya, cantaloupe, pear, smoked agave, toasted cedar, and jalapeño. Baked orange on first sip, then a surge of raw ginger heat, saline minerality, and pickle juice, before returning to gingersnaps, marmalade, and nutmeg. The finish tingles with ginger spice—invigorating, balanced, and precisely the type of innovation the Special Releases needed.

n: Laphroaig Càirdeas Lore Cask Strength (2025 Release), 59.6%
t: Lots of peat on the nose, then grilled bacon against potpourri, lavender, and back notes of vanilla and dark fruit. Smoke and dark fruit on the
f: Lots of peat on the nose, then grilled bacon against potpourri, lavender, and back notes of vanilla and dark fruit. Smoke and dark fruit on the palate, but it’s soft and sweet, with a nice peated bite. A very long finish, remarkably fruity and flavorful, with the peat continuing on along with maritime flavors of dried seaweed, sea salt, and brine. Racy and complex.

n: Parker’s Heritage Collection 11 year old (2025 Release), 61.25%
t: Peanuts, unbuttered popcorn, milk chocolate, chocolate frosting, vanilla, pipe tobacco, and sweet oak on a complex and very inviting nose. A thick,
f: Peanuts, unbuttered popcorn, milk chocolate, chocolate frosting, vanilla, pipe tobacco, and sweet oak on a complex and very inviting nose. A thick, rich mouthfeel—a bit hot but in control—with red berries, orange slices, chocolate, almond, coconut, baked cherries, and bitter espresso. The finish offers more red berries, veering toward rich dark chocolate. Great texture, delicious flavors, but perhaps somewhat dry on the back end. Best with a rock of ice.

t: Matured in new Appalachian oak casks, the nose is complex with black currant mousse, baked cherry, cake mix, toasted coconut, vanilla, candied
f: Matured in new Appalachian oak casks, the nose is complex with black currant mousse, baked cherry, cake mix, toasted coconut, vanilla, candied orange, allspice, and ground fennel. The clean supple texture is built around rye spices and Ryelaw’s wonderful signature black currant note. It opens with warming toffee and vanilla fudge, adding ginger, clove, nutmeg, and cinnamon, with sweet ginger and maple syrup on the finish.

t: A more accessibly priced bourbon from 15 Stars. Dry and herbal on the nose, with dark notes of fig and raisin beneath. The palate is mellow, with
f: A more accessibly priced bourbon from 15 Stars. Dry and herbal on the nose, with dark notes of fig and raisin beneath. The palate is mellow, with sweeter bakery and vanilla flavors emerging—cinnamon-sprinkled jelly doughnuts, vanilla custard, jammy red fruit, and powdered sugar nicely punctuated by spice. The finish continues the progression to a flavorful end. A pleasant sipper that will have you reaching for more.

t: Octomore in its purest form, aged entirely in first-fill bourbon barrels with no wine cask finishing. Pineapple, lime, sweet malt, apricot, and
f: Octomore in its purest form, aged entirely in first-fill bourbon barrels with no wine cask finishing. Pineapple, lime, sweet malt, apricot, and vanilla on the nose. The palate is smooth, with vanilla cookies and lemon cake against well-integrated peat and charcoal. The finish has great length, with lime and pineapple returning. Powerful but controlled, clean, and pure, showing complexity and maturity well beyond its 5-year age statement.

n: West Cork Maritime Release Rum Cask Finished, 46%
t: This opens with a gentle nose of stewed pears and spiced apple cider. With time, and a little swirl in the glass, deeper spice aromas emerge with
f: This opens with a gentle nose of stewed pears and spiced apple cider. With time, and a little swirl in the glass, deeper spice aromas emerge with clove and cinnamon featuring prominently. On the palate, the cask finish is more evident with vanilla, toasted coconut, and a hint of overripe bananas balanced by toasted barley and a hint of citrus. The finish shines, with vanilla, rum, and roasting coffee beans fading slowly.

n: Sons of Vancouver Realms of Rye 100% Rye (Release 01), 59.4%
t: This inaugural release in the Realms of Rye series was matured in bourbon barrels and new American oak. On the nose there’s orange blossom,
f: This inaugural release in the Realms of Rye series was matured in bourbon barrels and new American oak. On the nose there’s orange blossom, black tea, berries, and a whisper of roasted grain. The palate is spicier, with spiky cinnamon and dark chocolate. With water, it turns peppery and remains bold. The finish is long and nutty, with toasted walnuts and almonds

n: Cedar Ridge The QuintEssential Special Release Number Five Cask Strength (2025 Release), 58.9%
t: Exceptionally dark, this gets its color and character from spending time in five different barrels, including port and madeira. It’s lively on
f: Exceptionally dark, this gets its color and character from spending time in five different barrels, including port and madeira. It’s lively on the palate, delivering toasted pecan, raisin bread, and some peppery spice and maple sweetness. A little water makes it even better, amping up the sweetness and bringing balance to the liquid. A big, bold, and powerful whiskey with plenty of zing.

n: Loch Lomond The Open Course Special Edition 2025 Finished in Chianti Wine Casks, 46%
t: Finished in first-fill chianti casks for 8 months, the aromas unwrap red apple, pear, layers of caramel and malt, and gentle puffs of smoke. Pressed
f: Finished in first-fill chianti casks for 8 months, the aromas unwrap red apple, pear, layers of caramel and malt, and gentle puffs of smoke. Pressed apple juice, raspberry, red currant, baked pear, cinder toffee, vanilla, and soft smoke on the palate. The texture thickens beautifully, adding mellow flavors of dark chocolate and fruit pastilles. It’s a great session whisky, with a mouth-coating finish of cocoa-dusted orchard fruit.

n: Alexander Murray & Co. 2011 Teaninich 12 year old Orange County Soccer Club Single Cask (No. 723461), 52%
t: This rare bottling from one of Diageo’s workhorse distilleries shows off a Highland malt that typically ends up in blends. On the nose,
f: This rare bottling from one of Diageo’s workhorse distilleries shows off a Highland malt that typically ends up in blends. On the nose, there’s a banquet of fruits ranging from pineapple and a hint of passion fruit to ripe blackberries and blueberries. The palate is peppery, with a noticeable zing from the proof. It opens up with water, revealing honeyed oats and brioche, with lightly toasted oak on the finish.

n: Sagamore Spirit 7 year old Bottled in Bond (Batch 4A), 50%
t: As Sagamore’s bottled in bond Maryland ryes get older, their flavors grow in tandem. Baking spice, cinnamon applesauce, pie crust, and vanilla
f: As Sagamore’s bottled in bond Maryland ryes get older, their flavors grow in tandem. Baking spice, cinnamon applesauce, pie crust, and vanilla frosting fill the nose. On the palate, a delightful texture is supported by more baking spice, plus barrel char, baked apple, and Creamsicle. The finish is a decent length and veers toward darker, deeper notes of baking chocolate and more char.

t: From the distillery’s core range, aged in American and European oak, oloroso, and PX casks. Tarry barrel char, candied orange, vanilla-frosted
f: From the distillery’s core range, aged in American and European oak, oloroso, and PX casks. Tarry barrel char, candied orange, vanilla-frosted cupcake, and steeped black tea on the nose. The palate is soft and nicely spiced with baked apples, cinnamon, and a hint of banana. The long finish offers balanced pepper spice, more baked apple, blueberry pie, and a hint of cigar ash. Depth and length on the finish, with layered complexity.

t: For this single malt, Smokehead took its flagship whisky and finished it in tequila casks for 6 months. That agave influence isn’t immediately
f: For this single malt, Smokehead took its flagship whisky and finished it in tequila casks for 6 months. That agave influence isn’t immediately apparent, as the nose is dominated by yeasty aromas, stone fruit, graham cracker crust, lemon-coated apple, and of course, tendrils of peat smoke. The palate is pleasant, if a bit thin, with notes of lemon meringue, black pepper, and berries. There’s not an ounce of heat on the finish, but it’s honeyed and perfectly sippable, especially for those who might be scared of a peated whisky with bite.

t: This kicks off exquisitely, as aromas of ripe red berries, fresh apricot, mellow peat, and vanilla rise from the glass. The palate is viscous and
f: This kicks off exquisitely, as aromas of ripe red berries, fresh apricot, mellow peat, and vanilla rise from the glass. The palate is viscous and hot, but not overwhelmingly so, with heaps of spice tempered by strawberry puree, ginger, and char. Berry brightness sticks the landing, ensuring the finish is a gorgeous combination of fruit, spice, and smoke.

n: Royal Salute 21 year old Rio de Janeiro Polo Edition, 40%
t: Inspired by Brazil, a portion of this blend is aged in first-fill Braeval Distillery whisky casks to add fragrant floral notes. The nose brings
f: Inspired by Brazil, a portion of this blend is aged in first-fill Braeval Distillery whisky casks to add fragrant floral notes. The nose brings fresh-cut grass, florals, caramel, bright herbal notes, shredded coconut, mint leaf, and lime zest. Smooth and honeyed on the palate, it revolves around sweetened coconut, granola, vanilla, cinnamon cookies, salted caramel, and baked fruits, with a creamy sweet finish of Biscoff, mint, and spices.

t: The latest batch of this label that debuted in 2019 is a blend of three different recipes. Aromas of pine, licorice, and Earl Grey tea on the nose.
f: The latest batch of this label that debuted in 2019 is a blend of three different recipes. Aromas of pine, licorice, and Earl Grey tea on the nose. Sweet, malty, and with a syrupy mouthfeel on the palate that offers honey, golden raisins, vanilla, spice, chocolate, and a hint of coconut. More malt, spice, vanilla, and honey on a finish with good length. Pleasant malty sweetness—quite malty a times—with interesting flavors

n: Wheel Horse 4 year old Caribbean Rum Barrel Finished (2024 Release), 50.5%
t: This has a punchy nose of cherry cola, molasses, and caramel apple. On the palate, the influence of the rum barrel finish shows, with banana, cherry
f: This has a punchy nose of cherry cola, molasses, and caramel apple. On the palate, the influence of the rum barrel finish shows, with banana, cherry pie, and a little bit of funk mingling with the rye’s spicy cinnamon, maple, and apple flavor profile. There’s pepper, fennel, and a hint of mint interweaved with the sweeter flavors, giving the whiskey more depth. On the finish, the pepper lingers with charred oak and molasses.

n: Glenturret 7 year old Peat Smoked (2024 Release), 46%
t: A wonderful hit of peat, fatty barbecued meats, and spicy smoke on a very fragrant nose. Lots of balanced peat on the palate, along with baked red
f: A wonderful hit of peat, fatty barbecued meats, and spicy smoke on a very fragrant nose. Lots of balanced peat on the palate, along with baked red berries and dark chocolate—sweet but balanced against the peat. On the finish, it’s mid-length but very flavorful, a mix of dark chocolate and bright fruits, with peat fading in the distance. Not a hefty peat bomb in the least, despite the opening blast.

t: Matured in a combination of bourbon and madeira casks, the nose has lush layers of fruity sweetness, showing apple, mandarin, apricot syrup,
f: Matured in a combination of bourbon and madeira casks, the nose has lush layers of fruity sweetness, showing apple, mandarin, apricot syrup, raspberry, and a nip of dried chile flakes, mingled with heady florals and honey aromas. It’s complex and spicy on the palate, with chile heat chasing flavors of mandarin, toffee, candied citrus, and choco- late, ending with a mouth-coating finish of red apple, cherryade, and chocolate-dipped gingerbread. (Travel Retail exclusive; Release date: 8/24)

t: This first age-stated expression from The Sexton was aged in oloroso-seasoned French oak casks. It has swirling aromas of dark sherry fruit, with
f: This first age-stated expression from The Sexton was aged in oloroso-seasoned French oak casks. It has swirling aromas of dark sherry fruit, with dried vine fruit, fig, crème caramel, hazelnut, and peppercorn. The palate is fruity with a velvety texture, and boasts baked apple, plum, raisin, peppercorn, clove, freshly baked cookies, milk chocolate, and Brazil nut, and concludes with a smooth, flavorsome coffee bean finish. (Travel Retail exclusive; Release date: 1/25)

n: Bushmills 12 year old PX Sherry Cask Reserve, 46%
t: Initially matured in bourbon casks, this triple distilled single malt is finished in Pedro Ximénez sherry casks. It’s bright and appealing,
f: Initially matured in bourbon casks, this triple distilled single malt is finished in Pedro Ximénez sherry casks. It’s bright and appealing, with vanilla, caramel, dried apple, milk choco- late, and grapefruit peel oils on the nose. Condensed milk flavors make it sweet and creamy on first sip, with Horlicks, vanilla, caramel, apple ring, cranberry, and a hint of clove. The finish is dark and spicy with ginger- bread, coffee bean, and licorice allsorts. (Travel Retail exclusive; Release date 11/24)

t: Gaelic for “morning sky,” the recipe includes whiskies matured in French and Italian red wine casks. Jammy fruits and spice on the nose,
f: Gaelic for “morning sky,” the recipe includes whiskies matured in French and Italian red wine casks. Jammy fruits and spice on the nose, with bramble, raspberry, maritime notes, allspice, and clove. The palate abounds with fruity freshness, showing apple, orange, and fruit Life Savers, developing flavors of sweet honey, cashew, salted caramel, and candied orange, giving way to citrus peel and peat smoke on the finish. (Travel Retail exclusive; Release date: 2014) $89/liter

t: Matured in bourbon barrels for the full 18 years. The nose has sweet lemon, oiliness, and vanilla ice cream; overall, a lovely patisserie aroma
f: Matured in bourbon barrels for the full 18 years. The nose has sweet lemon, oiliness, and vanilla ice cream; overall, a lovely patisserie aroma underpinned by chalki- ness and minerality. The palate is luscious and fruity, with candied pineapple, sweet mango, baked cherries, apricot, and melon. Length and sweetness on the finish, but like the nose, it has great flavor variation and terrific balance between underlying minerality and sweet fruit. (Release date: 10/24)

t: Meaning “peat stack” in Gaelic, this heavily- peated expression is appealing and approachable with sweet peat on the nose, plus fresh
f: Meaning “peat stack” in Gaelic, this heavily- peated expression is appealing and approachable with sweet peat on the nose, plus fresh hay, custard creams, lime, vanilla short- bread, and candied lemons. Malted biscuits, honey, and watermelon on the palate are overcome by layers of peat smoke, pepper, and salty smoked fish, leading to a dry, smoky coastal saltiness with just a hint of candied fruit. (Travel Retail exclusive; Release date: 2010) $105/liter

n: Bushmills 2014 Private Reserve Series 10 year old Amarone Cask, 47.3%
t: Amarone is a new finishing cask for the second Bushmills Private Reserve Series, and delivers an enticing nose of red grape, cherry, dried fig, and
f: Amarone is a new finishing cask for the second Bushmills Private Reserve Series, and delivers an enticing nose of red grape, cherry, dried fig, and five spice. The palate is thick and fruity with cherry, bramble, clove, fresh plum, a touch of leather, and some late vanilla creaminess before a lengthy finish of ripe fruit, vanilla, and clove. Water opens it up beautifully, brightening the fruit notes. (Release date: 2/25)

n: Glen Scotia 9 year old Heavily Peated Ribera del Duero Finished (Campbeltown Malts Festival), 54.3%
t: Initially matured in first-fill bourbon barrels, this was finished in Spanish wine casks for 5-6 months. A mingling of smoke, dark fruits, maraschino
f: Initially matured in first-fill bourbon barrels, this was finished in Spanish wine casks for 5-6 months. A mingling of smoke, dark fruits, maraschino cherry, juicy red berries, vanilla wafer, peppercorn, and chocolaty peat smoke invade the nostrils. Beautiful expression of apple and raspberry fruit, the smoke more apparent after the alcohol peaks, retaining the smoke, then bold spices, creaminess, and fruit into the finish. Preferable with a dash of water. (Release date: 4/25)

n: Bushmills 15 year old Bourbon Cask Reserve, 46%
t: This triple distilled single malt comes from stocks matured in first and second-fill bourbon casks only. Lashings of vanilla on the nose, with honey,
f: This triple distilled single malt comes from stocks matured in first and second-fill bourbon casks only. Lashings of vanilla on the nose, with honey, coconut macaroon, butterscotch, and almond Florentines. The mouthfeel is silky and glossy, with vanilla, caramel, toffee apple, hazelnut, butterscotch, candied citrus, and gentle peppery spices. The finish has seasoned oak, nuts, and peppercorn. A very accom- plished whiskey with a delicious flavor profile (Travel Retail exclusive; Release date: 8/23)

n: Backbone Bourbon Triple Down Single Barrel Light Whiskey (2024 Release), 68.3%
t: Light whiskey sourced from MGP and bottled from a single barrel. On the nose, toffee, Tootsie Roll, chocolate-covered raspberries, and wool. Cherries
f: Light whiskey sourced from MGP and bottled from a single barrel. On the nose, toffee, Tootsie Roll, chocolate-covered raspberries, and wool. Cherries and raspberries on the palate, which needs water, coaxing out salt water taffy, marshmallow, vanilla almond ice cream, and coconut flakes. Lively, sweet flavors of ice cream shop and candy store. Nice length and sweetness on the finish, with waves of sweet vanilla and whipped cream, though a bit one-dimensional.

n: Sazerac 18 year old (Buffalo Trace Antique Collection 2024), 45%
t: A mainstay of the annual series, Sazerac 18 year old doesn’t vary too much year to year, keeping the same age, low-rye mashbill, and proof.
f: A mainstay of the annual series, Sazerac 18 year old doesn’t vary too much year to year, keeping the same age, low-rye mashbill, and proof. That said, the 2024 release finds a way to thrill, packing fresh spicy grain notes on the nose alongside eucalyptus, ripe cherries, and grape jelly. The palate is softer, and tantalizes with dark chocolate, tobacco ash, oak spice, and blueberries. A never-ending finish brings out the best of this rye, beautifully melding all the notes that came before. (Release date: 10/24)

n: Penelope 10 year old Estate Collection Single Barrel (2024 Release; Barrel No. 24-56), 49%,
t: Late last fall, Penelope released two different single barrel bottlings, with this one made from a 75% corn, 21% rye, and 4% malted barley; and its
f: Late last fall, Penelope released two different single barrel bottlings, with this one made from a 75% corn, 21% rye, and 4% malted barley; and its sister whiskey made from a mash of 60% corn, 36% rye, and 4% malted barley. On the nose, this lower-rye release leads with spiced caramel latte, vanilla poundcake, and gingersnaps. The flavors are fruitier, with apple cider and berry compote complementing the prickle of sweet chile peppers and cinnamon candies. (Release date: 10/24)

t: I’ll say it: This Beyoncé-owned whiskey is worth its salt. The nose is lightly spiced and fresh, with bright grain and clove
f: I’ll say it: This Beyoncé-owned whiskey is worth its salt. The nose is lightly spiced and fresh, with bright grain and clove complemented by fruitier notes of raisin and orange oil. Made from a mashbill of 51% rye and 49% malted barley, it’s mild-mannered as far as rye goes, gently led by a silky-smooth mouthfeel that brings sweeter flavors of dried cherries and candied nuts alongside earthier notes of rye bread. The finish wraps up on a flavorful, balanced note. (Release date: 9/24)

n: Angel’s Envy Triple Oak Hungarian, Chinkapin, & French Oak Barrel Finished, 46%
t: This is the first addition to Angel’s Envy’s core lineup since the release of its rum cask-finished rye in 2013. On the nose
f: This is the first addition to Angel’s Envy’s core lineup since the release of its rum cask-finished rye in 2013. On the nose there’s spiced oak, cherry cordials, and whipped cream, with an undercurrent of dried fruit. The palate offers brown sugar, salted caramel, and a prominent oak spiciness. Coffee, cigar leaf, and oak on the lengthy finish.

n: New Riff 7 year old Sour Mash (Fall 2024 Vatting), 57.25%
t: On the nose, the latest New Riff single malt is rife with trail mix, candied nuts, raisin bread, banana nut muffin, and bubble gum. While the palate
f: On the nose, the latest New Riff single malt is rife with trail mix, candied nuts, raisin bread, banana nut muffin, and bubble gum. While the palate is a tad thin at first brush, the flavors are robust and rousing: Dark chocolate ganache and chocolate-covered espresso beans mingle with dried cherries and a handful of crushed herbs. Whoppers, cinnamon, and blueberry maple syrup take center stage on the lengthy finish. (Release date: 8/24)

n: Johnnie Walker Blue Label Ice Chalet, 43%
t: Favoring whiskies distilled in winter at high-altitude scotch distilleries, this encapsulates the spirit of the north for that après-ski
f: Favoring whiskies distilled in winter at high-altitude scotch distilleries, this encapsulates the spirit of the north for that après-ski moment. Vanilla fudge, honeycomb, sultana, aniseed, and spicy herbal notes on the nose. It has a soft, supple texture on the palate, with flavors of red apple, blueberry, honey, vanilla, and glimpses of aniseed, ginger root, and menthol. A peppery blast on the finish, with smokiness hanging in the air. (Release date: 10/24).

t: This decade-old Basil Hayden entices early with a nose of fresh fruit: there’s green apple, applesauce, lemon juice, ripe Bosc pear, and
f: This decade-old Basil Hayden entices early with a nose of fresh fruit: there’s green apple, applesauce, lemon juice, ripe Bosc pear, and vanilla frosting. While the mouthfeel is a tad thin (a byproduct of lower proof) the palate is flavorful all the same, spotlighting baking spice, vanilla pudding cup, white pepper, honey, and the slightest hint of black coffee. Peppery spice, cinnamon, caramel swirl, and sugar cookie combine for a warming finish that lingers on for a while. (Release date: 9/24)

n: Glenmorangie A Tale of Ice Cream, 46%
t: Glenmorangie’s mad scientist Dr. Bill Lumsden and master blender Gillian Macdonald worked with whiskies aged in oak that was specially toasted
f: Glenmorangie’s mad scientist Dr. Bill Lumsden and master blender Gillian Macdonald worked with whiskies aged in oak that was specially toasted to draw out vanillin from the wood. The experiment worked: This whisky delivers a cornucopia of vanilla-inflected sweets, from ice cream to fudge to fresh whipped cream. The sweets are backed by a malty heart that shows honey, cinnamon, and a bit of custardy tang. (Release date: 10/24)

n: William Larue Weller (Buffalo Trace Antique Collection 2024), 62.9%
t: This year’s Antique Collection’s wheated bourbon lost 61% of its volume due to evaporation, according to Buffalo Trace. The significant
f: This year’s Antique Collection’s wheated bourbon lost 61% of its volume due to evaporation, according to Buffalo Trace. The significant loss of the angel’s share has created an incredibly concentrated and powerful whiskey. The nose pops from the glass with sweet corn, vanilla frosting, and rich spiced wood. The palate is bold and flavorful, with Mexican hot chocolate, mashmallow, and spiced fruits. The finish is long and robust. (Release date: 10/24).

n: The ImpEx Collection Benrinnes 12 year old Single Cask (No. 306532; distilled in 2011), 58.9%
t: Oak shavings, vanilla pod, and perfumed soaps on first sniff, then hints of chocolate, dried orange disc, and juicy peach. Initially, the palate has
f: Oak shavings, vanilla pod, and perfumed soaps on first sniff, then hints of chocolate, dried orange disc, and juicy peach. Initially, the palate has peach, apricot, and guava, swept aside by clove, nutmeg, and pepper, then pastrami bark, licorice, leather, and bramble. The finish offers clove, nutmeg, ginger, and tobacco. It’s true to the spirit of Benrinnes character if you know it well.

n: Mars Tsunuki Bakemono Zukushi Emaki No. 5 Minokedashi Single Cask Sherry Hogshead Matured, 60%
t: Beautifully balanced with well-integrated smoke and sand dune aromas, plus black cherry, raisin, chocolate, black currant mousse, and a rising note
f: Beautifully balanced with well-integrated smoke and sand dune aromas, plus black cherry, raisin, chocolate, black currant mousse, and a rising note of cranberry. This peated whisky excels at delivering chocolate-covered cherry flavors, with cranberries, clove, fig, date, and unsweetened chocolate, then residual smoke drifting into the finish of raisins and spicy fig. The high proof is noticeable, but even with plenty of water, it still delivers a flavorsome dram. (U.S. exclusive)

t: On the nose, raspberry, red apple, plum jam, currants, and Seville orange marmalade sit on a base of caramel and gentle spice. Warm and fruity on the
f: On the nose, raspberry, red apple, plum jam, currants, and Seville orange marmalade sit on a base of caramel and gentle spice. Warm and fruity on the palate, reminiscent of apples baked in brown sugar and golden syrup, then a darker phase of chocolate praline, clove, licorice, plum, and prune, where it resides in its wonderfully dark, plummy depths for the duration of the finish, remaining actively spicy for quite some time.

t: This peaty expression—despite its name it was not released until 2024—was matured in sherry casks and re-charred American oak Mellow
f: This peaty expression—despite its name it was not released until 2024—was matured in sherry casks and re-charred American oak Mellow Kozuru shochu casks. Salty seaweed, vanilla, chocolaty peat smoke, clove, antiseptic, and toasted raisin bread on the nose. Effortlessly drinkable at cask strength, with flavors of chocolate chip, raisin, cherry, and smoke, with sweeter milk chocolate, juicy sultana, and mixed peel notes emerging. The finish brings milk chocolate, cinnamon, and raspberry jam doughnut filling.

n: Mars Komagatake Bakemono Zukushi Emaki No. 1 Oyashirome Single Cask Bourbon Barrel Matured, 64%
t: Refreshing aromas of watermelon, ripening strawberry, ground pepper, cherry mochi, taffy, and a hint of kiwi. This comes in pretty hot on the palate,
f: Refreshing aromas of watermelon, ripening strawberry, ground pepper, cherry mochi, taffy, and a hint of kiwi. This comes in pretty hot on the palate, with strawberry, cranberry, Red Vines, pepper, red chile, baked apple, pear, raspberry, rowanberry, and a hint of chocolate. The fruit fades quickly in the finish, with water bringing out milk chocolate and quelling the heat and power of this cask-strength bottling. (U.S. exclusive)

t: A blend of three MGP high-rye bourbons. This is a big whiskey befitting the Babe. The nose hits hard with cherry pie, horchata, and chai spices. The
f: A blend of three MGP high-rye bourbons. This is a big whiskey befitting the Babe. The nose hits hard with cherry pie, horchata, and chai spices. The palate builds on those aromas, adding chocolate orange, ginger, and mint chocolate chip ice cream. Herbal and well spiced from nose to finish, it manages its proof with only a slight prickle on the palate. Anise and rye spices are prominent on the moderately long finish.

n: Mars Komagatake Bakemono Zukushi Emaki No. 4 Sarahebi Single Cask American White Oak Hogshead Matured, 60%,
t: The new oak delivers an amber-colored whisky with aromas of new leather, autumn leaves, peanuts, vanilla seeds, fresh oak, clove, and gingersnaps.
f: The new oak delivers an amber-colored whisky with aromas of new leather, autumn leaves, peanuts, vanilla seeds, fresh oak, clove, and gingersnaps. Flavors of orange taffy, sesame seed, peanut brittle, toasted granola, wood spices, peach cobbler, and the astringency of fresh oak make for a mouth-drawing experience. It benefits from a generous splash of water to overcome the dominant oak, which brings out the inherent fruitiness of the Komagatake distillate. (U.S. exclusive)

t: Cereal sweetness drifts from the glass, calling to mind Golden Grahams, cinnamon rugelach, cruller, pastry dough, cherry Danish, and a dollop of
f: Cereal sweetness drifts from the glass, calling to mind Golden Grahams, cinnamon rugelach, cruller, pastry dough, cherry Danish, and a dollop of honey. The soft, sugared flavors continue on the tremendously textured palate, though they’re livened up by peach preserves, bittersweet chocolate, and baking spice. A nice hit of cinnamon heat kicks off the finish, and cherry fruit notes become more pronounced, though the flavors remain well balanced.

t: The nose is gentle and rises from the glass almost tentatively with blackberries, tangerines, and peach preserves. A little time in the open air
f: The nose is gentle and rises from the glass almost tentatively with blackberries, tangerines, and peach preserves. A little time in the open air brings this one to life with deep aromas of pine forest, strawberry jelly, and subtle toasted oak. The palate is more pronounced, with Creamsicle, dried pineapple, and mint tea complementing the fruits first present on the nose. The finish is all vanilla sweetness and subdued oak

t: This heavily oaked version of Natterjack has sweet, rich aromas of heather honey, beeswax candles, vanilla, graham cracker, seasoned oak, and toasted
f: This heavily oaked version of Natterjack has sweet, rich aromas of heather honey, beeswax candles, vanilla, graham cracker, seasoned oak, and toasted coconut. Silky textured on the palate, with honey, vanilla, Creamsicle, Jaffa orange, toasted oak, and vanilla pod, becoming increasingly dry with gingersnap and licorice. Resinous oak, caramel, aniseed balls, and ginger on the finish. It makes a great introduction to Irish blends for bourbon diehards.

n: World Whiskey Society Wyatt Earp Single Barrel Cask Strength (Barrel No. 3B), 59.5%
t: Jammy and densely fruity, the nose leads with plums, Concord grape juice, and berry preserves, plus black pepper and a general spiciness aided by the
f: Jammy and densely fruity, the nose leads with plums, Concord grape juice, and berry preserves, plus black pepper and a general spiciness aided by the well-managed but noticeable proof. The palate offers more of the same with ripe fruits and banana bread, shortbread cookies, and vanilla extract. As the palate evolves, cinnamon, cloves, and nutmeg mingle with toasted grains for a long finish capped by bracing mint.

n: Four Roses Limited Edition Small Batch Barrel Strength (2024 Release), 54.1%
t: Sweet oak, vanilla, and rice pudding on the nose, with potpourri, dried herbs, incense, and a hint of barrel char. The palate offers more char,
f: Sweet oak, vanilla, and rice pudding on the nose, with potpourri, dried herbs, incense, and a hint of barrel char. The palate offers more char, melding with dark chocolate, unsweetened espresso, a tart bite, and more earthy notes of warehouse and oak. A balanced, spicy finish brings melted dark chocolate, camp coffee, cinnamon babka, and brown sugar as the flavors pour on. Superbly herbal, spicy, earthy, and chocolaty.

t: The nose has lots of sherry cask character, with black cherry, dried vine fruit, Seville orange peel, date, walnut, caramel, and a hint of dry
f: The nose has lots of sherry cask character, with black cherry, dried vine fruit, Seville orange peel, date, walnut, caramel, and a hint of dry spices. Moreish and delicious, it is rich and full on the palate, with black currant, chocolate, rye spice, plum, raisin, and hazelnut praline. The finish combines caramel, cinnamon, chocolate, and rye spice. Worth seeking out, as this won’t disappoint.

t: A beautiful combination of aromas, with honey, graham cracker, dried orange disc, mild spices, and gentle waves of chocolaty peat smoke. This carries
f: A beautiful combination of aromas, with honey, graham cracker, dried orange disc, mild spices, and gentle waves of chocolaty peat smoke. This carries through to the palate with melted milk chocolate, chewy toffee pepper, roasted spices, and black forest gateau, with the peat smoke present in the periphery. Absolutely delicious, this is a great peated Irish whiskey with a moreish finish of chocolate brownies and gentle bonfire smoke.

n: Nc’nean AON First Fill Bourbon Single Cask (No. 18-642), 60.4%
t: A symphony of stone fruit, apples, and pears greets the nose: Golden Delicious apple skin, apple tart, and juicy pear are well matched with vanilla
f: A symphony of stone fruit, apples, and pears greets the nose: Golden Delicious apple skin, apple tart, and juicy pear are well matched with vanilla soft serve and a hint of anise. On the palate, the texture is fantastic, offering up a wonderfully creamy mouthfeel that’s accented by flavors of juicy apricot, raw honey, and sugar cookie. The finish is spicy—think chocolate-covered chiles and brown sugar Pop-Tart. Water, while not needed, yields yogurt-covered pretzels and more fruit.

n: Royal Salute 21 year old The Miami Polo Edition, 40%
t: Perfect over ice for lazy hot days on the beach, the aromas revolve around caramel, vanilla, dry spices, creamy coconut, and burlap, plus some honey
f: Perfect over ice for lazy hot days on the beach, the aromas revolve around caramel, vanilla, dry spices, creamy coconut, and burlap, plus some honey and oak shavings. Melon and vanilla on the palate, with robust spiciness under the tongue, sliding into honey-baked pastries with toasted rye grain, and a finish of honey biscuits and mint leaf. This is creamy but substantial and offers plenty of spice and depth.

n: Single Malts of Scotland Linkwood 14 year old (Distilled in 2009), 55.8%
t: A charming nose of vanilla sponge, apple blossom, hay, white pepper, green apple, and lemon mousse with a hint of peach captures the best of
f: A charming nose of vanilla sponge, apple blossom, hay, white pepper, green apple, and lemon mousse with a hint of peach captures the best of Linkwood’s classic profile. The texture is glossy and glides across the tongue with flavors of lemon shortbread, sesame oil, white chocolate, clove, vanilla, and butter scotch. Water brings out its fruitier side, showcasing the lemon and green apple notes in particular.

n: Gold Spot 13 year old Generations Edition, 46%
t: The second release in the series, matured in sherry casks and finished 16 months in Recioto della Valpolicella casks. This is deliciously oily on the
f: The second release in the series, matured in sherry casks and finished 16 months in Recioto della Valpolicella casks. This is deliciously oily on the nose with cooked dark fruit, red grape, apple, peppercorn, cinnamon bark, and dusty oak. Thick and full-bodied with red apple, citrus peel, and pot still spices, supported by toasted oak leading to brown sugar, roasted nuts, and a superb pot still oiliness on the palate. The finish has sweet dried apple, oak, and lingering spices.

n: Single Malts of Scotland Aultmore 15 year old (Distilled in 2009), 60.7%
t: Bramble, black currant, baked plum, dunnage earthiness, and roasted spices exude from the glass, with the dark fruits proving to be quite punchy at
f: Bramble, black currant, baked plum, dunnage earthiness, and roasted spices exude from the glass, with the dark fruits proving to be quite punchy at this proof. Thick dark fruits on the palate too, in particular plum, black cherry, and red wine notes handing control to the spices, then oak tannins, black currant, and clove lead into the finish

n: Ezra Brooks 99 Special Cask Finished Series Port Wine Cask Finished, 49.5%
t: Quite a fruity start, as blackberry preserves, PB&J, and lemon rise from the glass. The palate is hot and packed with more berry fruit, though
f: Quite a fruity start, as blackberry preserves, PB&J, and lemon rise from the glass. The palate is hot and packed with more berry fruit, though there are herbaceous elements to parse out as well: spearmint, licorice, and cherry cough drop. With water, the heat’s been wrangled and brings out creamy chocolate. The mid-length finish has chocolate raspberry truffles and a pleasant honeyed sweetness.

t: From nose to finish, this is a roadside fruit stand, bringing fresh fruit, oak, and dusty earth together in harmony. The nose leads with sour
f: From nose to finish, this is a roadside fruit stand, bringing fresh fruit, oak, and dusty earth together in harmony. The nose leads with sour cherries, Concord grape juice, and a bevy of tropical fruits. The palate is rich with notes of pineapple, apple, and POG juice, then a heavy pour of Velvet Falernum adds to all the fruit flavors Dustiness and dry oak add a layer of complexity to each sip.

n: Little Book Chapter 8: Path Not Taken Blend of Straight Whiskeys (2024 Release), 59.10%
t: This rye-bourbon blend is master distiller Freddie Noe’s first effort at working with a range of ryes. Caramel, leather, fragrant oak, peach
f: This rye-bourbon blend is master distiller Freddie Noe’s first effort at working with a range of ryes. Caramel, leather, fragrant oak, peach tart, and warm bakery aromas on a complex nose. The palate is lush and fruity, while also offering baked fruit tart and lip-smacking rye spice. The finish is long and spicy—water is recommended, and it also brings out sweet vanilla and dried orange. An interesting rye departure in this series.

n: Keeper’s Heart 10 year old Malaga Wine Cask Finished, 43%
t: Orange and lemon peel, then a citric nose with splashes of vanilla frosting and drying oak. Creamy vanilla leads on a smooth palate, along with brown
f: Orange and lemon peel, then a citric nose with splashes of vanilla frosting and drying oak. Creamy vanilla leads on a smooth palate, along with brown sugar and oatmeal cookies, accented by balanced pepperoncini spice. The finish is long and flavorful, with orange returning, melding with vanilla custard, peppery spice, and sweet oak. This one can stand with many quality single malts, having great flavor progression from nose to finish.

n: Barrell Bourbon Cask Finish Series: Mizunara 6 year old blend of straights (Batch 001), 58.21%
t: The dry, aromatic nose is somewhat closed but aridly pleasant. On the palate, vanilla and jammy red berries are sprinkled with pepper spice and
f: The dry, aromatic nose is somewhat closed but aridly pleasant. On the palate, vanilla and jammy red berries are sprinkled with pepper spice and fragrant drying oak, creating balance. The finish is the best part—long, spicy, and earthy, with dark chocolate, tiramisu, and cinnamon. There is pronounced dryness here from the oak influence, but the flavors emerge after a time, even if they’re somewhat constricted.

n: Dewar’s 19 year old The Champion’s Edition (2024), 43%
t: Finished in rye casks for the 124th U.S. Open, the nose presents honey, green and toasted rye, rye crackers, and a subtle pepperiness. A fine blend
f: Finished in rye casks for the 124th U.S. Open, the nose presents honey, green and toasted rye, rye crackers, and a subtle pepperiness. A fine blend with flavors of caramel, poached pear, and rich vanilla, plus wood spice, cinnamon, and heather honey. Golden raisin and other dried fruits, with rye spice, vanilla, and a hint of cocoa on the finish.

t: This year’s Ardbeg Day release, using whiskies aged 9-13 years, 35% matured in bourbon barrels and the rest in port casks. A peat blast on the
f: This year’s Ardbeg Day release, using whiskies aged 9-13 years, 35% matured in bourbon barrels and the rest in port casks. A peat blast on the nose, softened by tart and sweet notes of lemon. The palate is peated and spicy, with Golden Delicious apples, honey, cracked pepper, charcoal, candle wax, and light soapiness. The finish is long, with apple, smoke, and honey, ending with subtle pepper spice. Spectacular is aptly named. No. 11 in our Top 20 of 2024 .

t: Stone fruit, strawberry ice cream bar, lemon peel, and a touch of grassiness make for an appealing nose. Creamy vanilla comes forth on the palate,
f: Stone fruit, strawberry ice cream bar, lemon peel, and a touch of grassiness make for an appealing nose. Creamy vanilla comes forth on the palate, which is hot, hot, hot, but not unpleasantly so, as it’s tied to notes of candied ginger and peppery spice. With water (which is definitely recommended for this one), the flavors expand considerably, revealing more vanilla, white pepper, and ample chocolate. The finish is splendid, rife with crème brûlée sweetness, graham cracker, and mocha.

n: Ammunition Cask Strength Cabernet Sauvignon Barrel Finished, 55%
t: The nose has a pleasant mustiness and woodiness about it, like being in an old attic. Eventually, these woody notes are complemented by brighter
f: The nose has a pleasant mustiness and woodiness about it, like being in an old attic. Eventually, these woody notes are complemented by brighter scents of candied orange, dried strawberries, and sliced banana. The palate is quite hot, and not for the faint of heart, but there are flavors galore to appreciate: orange chocolate truffle, Big Red gum, clove, and walnut share the spotlight. The creamy, lengthy finish yields candied nuts, cinnamon stick, and chocolate fudge.

n: Little Rest Double Matured Cask Strength, 62.6%
t: From New York’s Tenmile Distillery. The nose is quite earthy to start, yielding licorice, cloves, anise, and a packet of dried herbs. With
f: From New York’s Tenmile Distillery. The nose is quite earthy to start, yielding licorice, cloves, anise, and a packet of dried herbs. With time, sweeter aromas come forth: peach rings, blueberry-maple syrup, vanilla extract, and blueberry-lemon scone. Have tissues on hand for the palate; it’s an eye-watering experience, but beneath the heat are a beautiful texture and bounty of flavors, ranging from baking chocolate and brownie batter to leather and pecans. Cherry-dipped chocolate soft serve, cocoa powder, and raspberry coulis conclude the journey (which improves with water).

t: A summer barbecue on the nose: Meaty smoke, charcoal grill, burnt ends, and charred hot dogs pull you in. Soon enough, there’s a zip of
f: A summer barbecue on the nose: Meaty smoke, charcoal grill, burnt ends, and charred hot dogs pull you in. Soon enough, there’s a zip of blackberry jam and grape hard candy, with a hint of vanilla bean. The palate is delightfully creamy, abundant in fluffernutter sweetness, cinnamon baked apple, and a sizzle of jalapeño spice. The finish is round and long-lasting and delivers caramelized sugar, cooked raspberries, and Black Forest cake.

t: Peat smoke and charred pine aromas rise from the glass with crackling-ember intensity. The smoke is the star on the nose but it’s perfumed with
f: Peat smoke and charred pine aromas rise from the glass with crackling-ember intensity. The smoke is the star on the nose but it’s perfumed with charred pineapple and ripe lemons. After acclimating to the smoke, a medicinal character emerges with a hint of antiseptic, rubber, and Band-Aids vying with cedar smoke and citrus. The palate is long and sweetens with time, as vanilla and Creamsicle meet the considerable peaty punch.

n: Hard Truth Master Distiller’s Reserve Malted Rye Barrel Strength Sweet Mash (Batch 002), 56.7%
t: Made from a mash of 54% unmalted and 46% malted rye, this is assertive and loud from nose to finish. The nose is all earth and spice: cardamom,
f: Made from a mash of 54% unmalted and 46% malted rye, this is assertive and loud from nose to finish. The nose is all earth and spice: cardamom, cinnamon, damp leaves, and caramel candies. The high proof is well integrated on each sip, with this weighty whiskey delivering vanilla extract, high-cacao dark chocolate, French toast with maple syrup, and citrus slice candies.

n: Hard Truth 5 year old Bottled in Bond Sweet Mash Wheated (Spring 2019 Vintage), 50%
t: A mature 5 year old old from Indiana craft distiller Hard Truth. Dry and closed on the nose, but the palate offers sweet flavors of sugared
f: A mature 5 year old old from Indiana craft distiller Hard Truth. Dry and closed on the nose, but the palate offers sweet flavors of sugared raspberries and strawberries. Very fruited overall, with pleasant interplay between fruit and chocolate. It all concludes with a full-flavored finish that features more chocolate and a hint of ginger spice. Overall the chocolate wins out, resulting in a dessert-sweet yet oak-balanced whiskey.

t: Sriracha ketchup, muted bramble, and old leather on initial nosing, with emerging notes of sweet pickle and green chiles. Ripe nectarine, strawberry,
f: Sriracha ketchup, muted bramble, and old leather on initial nosing, with emerging notes of sweet pickle and green chiles. Ripe nectarine, strawberry, black grape, and dark sherry on the palate, the fruit concentrated but unsweetened, evolving to show plum, balsamic vinegar, leather, soy sauce, pickled walnut, and oak. Complex and distinctive, its idiosyncrasies will delight hardcore Japanese rice whisky fans, but the newly curious might want to sip before they commit. (2,324 bottles)

t: This whiskey was distilled in Kentucky, and spent 5 years aging there before embarking on a transatlantic journey to the UK. While it’s tough
f: This whiskey was distilled in Kentucky, and spent 5 years aging there before embarking on a transatlantic journey to the UK. While it’s tough to say how much said journey impacted the final whiskey, there’s certainly a lot of flavor to suss out here; the nose is fragrant with Dole fruit cup, cornbread, and cooked cherries. On the palate, the wonderfully round mouthfeel precedes more fruit flavors, plus some rich chocolate and barrel char. The finish leads with wood spice, chocolate, and cherry.

n: Aberfeldy 21 year old Argentinian Malbec Wine Cask Finish, 46%
t: Dark chocolate, ripe cherries, clove, and evolving notes of kaffir lime leaves and sprigs of fresh rosemary. Flavors of soft cooked fruits, toffee,
f: Dark chocolate, ripe cherries, clove, and evolving notes of kaffir lime leaves and sprigs of fresh rosemary. Flavors of soft cooked fruits, toffee, vanilla, honey-coated mixed nuts, black currant purée, ginger root, cinnamon, and hints of citrus before finally settling on a vanilla caramel note. The finish is long, with red apple, vanilla, and peppercorn. From a robust wine, the ginger and spice flavor indicate this finishing cask has produced an equally robust whisky.

t: This core expression offers aromas of rasp berry jam, baked orange, plum, peppercorn, dry autumn leaves, and a hint of leather, making it an
f: This core expression offers aromas of rasp berry jam, baked orange, plum, peppercorn, dry autumn leaves, and a hint of leather, making it an attractive prospect among the various 12 year old sherried Speyside single malt options around. Medium-bodied and juicy, with summer red berries, baked orange, vanilla, ripe cherry, marmalade, and gentle peppery spices, the flavors round off with aniseed, strawberry, and cherry lip balm.

n: Garrison Brothers Guadalupe Port Cask Finished (2024 Release), 53.5%
t: Very dark amber in color, which is fairly distinctive and apparent. Fortified wine notes of earthy dark sweetness, with torched marshmallow, dunnage
f: Very dark amber in color, which is fairly distinctive and apparent. Fortified wine notes of earthy dark sweetness, with torched marshmallow, dunnage warehouse floor, and spent barrel on the nose. The palate shows some rancio—adding an almost rustic but appealing presence—dark baked berries, chocolate, and sherry cooking wine. A lot of interesting flavors, including some very intriguing burnt berry notes on the finish, but overall unusually tasty.

n: High N’ Wicked 15 year old No.8 The Jury Madeira Cask Finished, 52%
t: After 14 years in new oak and 1 year in madeira casks, the verdict is in: This whiskey is opulent and weighty, with a nose of cherry pie,
f: After 14 years in new oak and 1 year in madeira casks, the verdict is in: This whiskey is opulent and weighty, with a nose of cherry pie, sarsaparilla, and bracing ash. Raspberry jam and dark chocolate lead the sip with chile pepper spice and charred bell peppers in support. With time, the whiskey’s sweeter elements take center stage, with cherry cordials and cinnamon candies leading to a long dark chocolaty finish buttressed by charred oak.

n: Filmland Spirits Ryes of the Robots Extended Cut Cask Strength, 54%
t: The nose is bursting with scents of brunch— monkey bread, cinnamon, powdered sugar on pancakes, vanilla sweetness, and lemon poppyseed muffin.
f: The nose is bursting with scents of brunch— monkey bread, cinnamon, powdered sugar on pancakes, vanilla sweetness, and lemon poppyseed muffin. Coffee comes forth on the palate, as rich notes of caramel macchiato, coffee ice cream, vanilla bean, and strawberry jam coat the mouth. This whiskey does a fine job holding its proof, and with water, the finish is flush with fruitier notes, plus a bit of chocolate and black coffee

t: Aromas of musty oak, old library books, broiled peaches, ladyfinger cookies, and a hint of tobacco on a mellow nose. The palate offer bitter
f: Aromas of musty oak, old library books, broiled peaches, ladyfinger cookies, and a hint of tobacco on a mellow nose. The palate offer bitter chocolate, but also sweet flavors of warm peach tart, crème brûlée, and lemon pie, with a dash of jalapeño pepper spice. The finish is very long, offering vanilla custard sprinkled with chocolate flakes and cinnamon. Very well-integrated with deep, layered flavor creating a sublime whisky.

t: Aromas of tantalizing citrus peels, rich vanilla toffee, zested lime, dried flowers, sliced pear, and hints of coffee, cinnamon, and nutmeg. The pot
f: Aromas of tantalizing citrus peels, rich vanilla toffee, zested lime, dried flowers, sliced pear, and hints of coffee, cinnamon, and nutmeg. The pot still spices are well integrated but play quite subtly in this vintage. The palate offers a light tropical fruitiness, plus nectarine, grape, papaya, citrus zest, spun sugar, vanilla, and American oak characteristics of honey, nutmeg, and toasted oak. A shift in flavor on the finish offers refreshment and zingy fruitiness akin to the 2018 vintage.

n: Hard Truth Master Distiller’s Reserve Chocolate Malt Barrel Strength Sweet Mash (Batch 002), 57.4%
t: Hard Truth’s second batch of this rye is a bakery in a bottle, opening with a sweet and bready nose spiked with cinnamon, well-done toast, and
f: Hard Truth’s second batch of this rye is a bakery in a bottle, opening with a sweet and bready nose spiked with cinnamon, well-done toast, and a little bit of char. On the palate there’s honey-wheat pretzels, cherry pie, and tiramisu. Water brings out fresher fruit flavors like Bing cherries, raspberry jam, and pears. The finish is long and balanced with chocolate cake sweetness tempered by clove and pepper spice.

t: Matured in bourbon, new charred oak, and rye barrels, the nose has toasted grains, chestnut flour, honey, soft peach, and toasted
f: Matured in bourbon, new charred oak, and rye barrels, the nose has toasted grains, chestnut flour, honey, soft peach, and toasted coconut strips. Peach and mango on the palate, with black pepper, cinnamon, nutmeg, rye spice, and a hint of dill followed by citrus, marzipan, and toasted oak. Overall, it’s gentle, fruity, and layered with toasty rye character. Candied orange and lingering spices on the finish.

t: Through and through, this is full of Southern culinary delights. On the nose there’s pecan pie and cornbread, berry cobbler, and baked apples,
f: Through and through, this is full of Southern culinary delights. On the nose there’s pecan pie and cornbread, berry cobbler, and baked apples, all carried by a backbone of oak. Summer strawberries, berries and whipped cream, and vanilla pound cake make for sweet flavors that evolve with pepper and herbs on the back palate.
