The finish takes its time and fades gently with more vanilla and oak.

n: Method and Madness Finished in Virgin Garryana Oak Barrels, 46%
t: Honey, vanilla, golden sultana, baked pastries, shortbread, lightly toasted oak, and lemon frosting on the nose. It’s very sweet on the palate,
f: Honey, vanilla, golden sultana, baked pastries, shortbread, lightly toasted oak, and lemon frosting on the nose. It’s very sweet on the palate, with golden syrup on porridge, citrus peel, clove, and oak. It’s mouth drawing and feels much higher strength than 46%, then finishes with honeycomb and toffee apple notes. (4,500 bottles)

n: Redwood Empire Devils Tower High Rye (Batch 001), 49.50%
t: Four-grain, high-rye bourbon blended from 25 barrels. Made from a mashbill of 51% corn, 45% rye, 2% wheat, and 2% malt, and then aged for at least 5
f: Four-grain, high-rye bourbon blended from 25 barrels. Made from a mashbill of 51% corn, 45% rye, 2% wheat, and 2% malt, and then aged for at least 5 years in toasted char No.-3 barrels. The nose is sweet and redolent of fragrant wood, followed by a palate filled with vanilla cream and chocolate syrup,  balanced by drying oak tannins. (6,000 bottles)

n: Kaiyo Wood Library Series The Ramu 8 year old Rum Barrel Finish, 46%
t: The rum cask finish complements the effects of the mizunara aging, producing a more sophisticated array of flavors than expected. The nose brings
f: The rum cask finish complements the effects of the mizunara aging, producing a more sophisticated array of flavors than expected. The nose brings vanilla frosting, light caramel, incense, aromatic spices, flaked almond, citrus peel oils, and hints of tropical fruit. Sweet melon, honey, lemon juice, grapefruit peel, vanilla, rum-raisin ice cream, and a deep well of spices on the palate, followed by honeyed mizunara notes, vanilla custard, candied orange, buttery fudge, and lemon shortbread.

t: Highly distinctive aromas abound; this is savory and spicy, with peanut, tonkatsu ramen, and bok choy, with a little graham cracker sweetness, black
f: Highly distinctive aromas abound; this is savory and spicy, with peanut, tonkatsu ramen, and bok choy, with a little graham cracker sweetness, black pepper, and aromatic spices. On the palate, there’s a soft baked sweetness, and a terrific spicy crescendo followed by golden syrup, almond sugar cookie, cinnamon, sliced cold roast beef, and mushroom. The finish offers cinnamon and cacao. This is what interesting grain whisky should be all about.

n: Widow Jane 13 year old Lucky Thirteen Blend of Straights (Batch 33), 46.5%
t: Fresh ripe cherries on the nose, along with pleasant wafts of vanilla bean, chocolate syrup, cherry-dipped chocolate soft serve, Pocky chocolate
f: Fresh ripe cherries on the nose, along with pleasant wafts of vanilla bean, chocolate syrup, cherry-dipped chocolate soft serve, Pocky chocolate biscuit sticks, and chocolate graham crackers. The palate is beautifully textured and loaded with chocolate, cacao nibs, s’mores, chocolate cherries, and the slightest bit of campfire char. The finish happily continues this journey of chocolate and cherries, and boy does it linger.

t: Composed of new oak, bourbon, refill, and sherry casks, the nose has fruitcake, dates, black tea, dried sage, and subtle mixed spices under a broad
f: Composed of new oak, bourbon, refill, and sherry casks, the nose has fruitcake, dates, black tea, dried sage, and subtle mixed spices under a broad canopy of breezy smoke. Syrupy sweet date and plum meet a burst of peppery spices, settling to a combination of herbal flavors, candied chestnut, sugared plum, and sultana, with a hint of vanilla and a mouth-coating finish of aniseed and herbal notes.

t: The nose offers chocolate, heather, earthy forest floor, ginger spice, and cherry. The palate is laden with lively fruit, fresh raspberries, and
f: The nose offers chocolate, heather, earthy forest floor, ginger spice, and cherry. The palate is laden with lively fruit, fresh raspberries, and mature oak. Not a lot of ABV to the backbone, but a very tasty balance between red berries, some earthiness, and just a light hint of char. The length is good on a fruity, flavorful finish that shows the beauty of a lighter dram.

n: Meikle Tòir The Sherry One 5 year old, 48%
t: Chocolate brownie, smoked orange disc, ground cumin, mild smoked paprika, gentle peat smoke, and a dusting of cocoa on the nose of this gem of a
f: Chocolate brownie, smoked orange disc, ground cumin, mild smoked paprika, gentle peat smoke, and a dusting of cocoa on the nose of this gem of a whisky matured in Pedro Ximénez and oloroso sherry puncheons. On the palate, dark chocolate slides in with smoke, blackberry, burnt sugar, treacle, espresso, maple-coated pecans, and sizzling spices. Melted chocolate, peat smoke, plum skins, and baked orange on the finish.

t: This is a full-on sherry lover’s whisky, with a nose of chocolate, dried fig, blood orange, chewy fruit bars, vine fruit, and warming spices.
f: This is a full-on sherry lover’s whisky, with a nose of chocolate, dried fig, blood orange, chewy fruit bars, vine fruit, and warming spices. It begins lightly on the taste buds with chocolate orange, malt, baked fruits, fruitcake, and pepper, then spins into baked orange, red apple, vanilla essence, and milk chocolate. A smooth creamy finish presents subtle spice with a touch of leather.

t: Raspberry tart, strawberries, pipe tobacco, candle wax, sweet baked apple, and orange on the nose. The palate is sweet but balanced by the oak, with
f: Raspberry tart, strawberries, pipe tobacco, candle wax, sweet baked apple, and orange on the nose. The palate is sweet but balanced by the oak, with more berries, savory spice, and chocolate. It’s very flavorful and completed by a long finish of red berries, well-integrated oak, and lots of spice. The sweetness is pronounced but does not go overboard, staying in balance with all else.

n: Shelter Point Smoke Point Single Malt, 53%
t: The nose is red-blooded: there’s new leather, tobacco smoke, cigar shavings, and leftover campfire coals. Warm bread pudding balances those
f: The nose is red-blooded: there’s new leather, tobacco smoke, cigar shavings, and leftover campfire coals. Warm bread pudding balances those deeper aromas, making for a pleasant ride. Mocha latte and deliciously smooth chocolate on the palate, along with a sprinkle of toasted coconut. Dark and roasty on the finish, calling to mind dark chocolate-covered espresso beans, burnt coffee, and campfire smoke.

t: Orange peel, light vanilla, a few floral notes, and a dusting of aromatic spices. Nothing wrong with it, but nothing to get excited about either.
f: Orange peel, light vanilla, a few floral notes, and a dusting of aromatic spices. Nothing wrong with it, but nothing to get excited about either. Thin, lacking in body, with a sweet granular texture and flavors of clementine, vanilla sugar, caramel, and red apple. A vanilla sweetness on the finish, but there’s a bit of a burn as this goes down.

n: Old Dominick 5 year old Bottled in Bond (Fall 2017 Vintage), 50%
t: Red fruit galore on the nose, as cherries, pomegranate, and berries waft from the glass. A pleasant undercurrent of milk chocolate and cherry cola
f: Red fruit galore on the nose, as cherries, pomegranate, and berries waft from the glass. A pleasant undercurrent of milk chocolate and cherry cola makes the aromas that much more enticing. On the palate, grape jelly, raspberry Linzer cookie, chocolate jellies, and chocolate dipped strawberries. More chocolate on the finish, which builds to encompass rich flavor of mocha latte, toasted nuts, chocolate layer cake, and cacao.

n: Pokeno Exploration Series No. 01 Totara Cask, 46%
t: Finished in 200-liter totara casks—a hard, straight-grained indigenous wood—the nose has toasted coconut, cinnamon bark, macaroons,
f: Finished in 200-liter totara casks—a hard, straight-grained indigenous wood—the nose has toasted coconut, cinnamon bark, macaroons, fragrant floral notes, mint leaf, lemon hard candies, pear, peach, and light honey. Lemon, white chocolate, dried stone and tropical fruits, caramel, and toasted spices, with creaminess, malt, and milk chocolate breaking out in the end. Lightly structured on first sip, but it develops more body given time.

t: Bottled at hazmat proof, this is as untamed as the Wild West and, without water, as withering as the desert sun. The nose is dense and spicy with
f: Bottled at hazmat proof, this is as untamed as the Wild West and, without water, as withering as the desert sun. The nose is dense and spicy with cinnamon, sarsaparilla, dark chocolate, and cloves. Even with ample water added, it is rich and oily, with prominent oak, lemon, orange, and black pepper flavors. The finish is long, with vanilla sweetness, cinnamon tang, and parched oak.

t: GlenDronach is one of Scotland’s oldest whisky distilleries, dating back to 1826, but it has been sold, shuttered, and resold several times.
f: GlenDronach is one of Scotland’s oldest whisky distilleries, dating back to 1826, but it has been sold, shuttered, and resold several times. Its return to production in 2002 was great news for scotch lovers, and today it’s under the direction of Brown-Forman master blender Dr. Rachel Barrie. This newest iteration is a bold, memorable cask strength, sherry-matured whisky that comes alive in the glass with chewy, zippy notes of leather, cedar, and honey, then a wisp of flinty gun - powder accents the sweet finish. This sherry-finished scotch is the kind of drink that cries out for a beautiful cigar on a cold winter night.  No.-10 Top 20 of 2023

t: A giant of a whisky, with the highest proof ever on our Top 20 list, Highland Park Cask Strength is about more than just high-octane thrills.
f: A giant of a whisky, with the highest proof ever on our Top 20 list, Highland Park Cask Strength is about more than just high-octane thrills. Unencumbered by an age statement, master whisky maker Gordon Motion was free to paint Batch 4 with flavor in mind, using a vivid palette of sherry-seasoned European and American oak, bourbon, and refill casks, then in a twist, adding port casks for a daring new streak of flavor. In the distillery’s 225th year, Motion’s stellar accomplishment integrates expressive notes of pink grapefruit and exotic spices within a deep well of citrus, dark chocolate, and heathery peat smoke.  No.-2 Top 20 Whiskies of 2023

n: Grey Coast American Oak Cask Finished, 40%
t: 88 , $37 All sorts of lemon on the nose: lemon pound cake, lemon-poppyseed muffin, and lemon frosting. There’s some char as well, accented by
f: 88 , $37 All sorts of lemon on the nose: lemon pound cake, lemon-poppyseed muffin, and lemon frosting. There’s some char as well, accented by sawdust and a fruity wave of hibiscus iced tea. The palate is light, but there’s an oaky chardonnay roundness here that’s rich in both butter and butterscotch. The finish is creamy, following the path outlined on the palate.—JH

n: Claxton’s Inchfad 5 year old Oloroso Sherry Hogshead, 50%
t: The smoke on this peated whisky from Loch Lomond Distillery is woody, like burning old seasoned logs, and joins gentle notes of cherry, orchard
f: The smoke on this peated whisky from Loch Lomond Distillery is woody, like burning old seasoned logs, and joins gentle notes of cherry, orchard fruit, peppermint, allspice, and Brazil nutshells. Apple, butterscotch, vanilla, white chocolate, clove, and pepper on the palate, with hints of coffee, showing more orchard fruit as it dilutes. The fruit truly shines in this young whisky with the addition of a few drops of water. (72 bottles)

n: Four Roses Limited Edition Small Batch 135th Anniversary (2023), 54%
t: Nicely herbal on the nose, with overtones of vanilla and a hint of tobacco leaf adding to the overall fragrance. The palate is deliciously creamy,
f: Nicely herbal on the nose, with overtones of vanilla and a hint of tobacco leaf adding to the overall fragrance. The palate is deliciously creamy, with whipped cream, a hint of citrus, orange slices, warm brownies, a light nuttiness, and more tobacco leaf on the back palate. Plenty of spice and grip, with water adding dark chocolate and black coffee. A quality dram that hits all the bells—length, depth, complexity, and sheer enjoyability.

n: Rossville Union 6 year old Bottled in Bond (2023), 50%
t: The nose is bright and fruity, pulling you in with apricot, fresh orange slices, banana bread, oatmeal raisin cookie, and maple brown sugar oatmeal.
f: The nose is bright and fruity, pulling you in with apricot, fresh orange slices, banana bread, oatmeal raisin cookie, and maple brown sugar oatmeal. The richly textured palate is rife with more cinnamon spice, but there’s also a great deal of toffee, Heath bar, and double chocolate brownies, making for a glass that’s hard to put down. More chocolate on the finish, in the form of no-bake brownies and cacao nibs, as well as baked apples and honeyed sweetness.

t: A beautiful and balanced nose of chocolate, ashy smoke, malt, granola bars, hot coals, burlap coffee sacks, and a hint of creosote-painted fence. The
f: A beautiful and balanced nose of chocolate, ashy smoke, malt, granola bars, hot coals, burlap coffee sacks, and a hint of creosote-painted fence. The familiar Waterford fruit salad notes show on the palate, with watermelon, cherry, red grape, and red apple, then pepper and salty peat smoke rounding off with chocolate pudding, hints of soy sauce, and rich chocolaty smoke. If anything, water jacks up the flavors to new levels of intensity.

t: A crack of black pepper, a little cassis, lemon-poppyseed muffin, vanilla pudding, Frosted Flakes, and a dollop of honey point the nose in an
f: A crack of black pepper, a little cassis, lemon-poppyseed muffin, vanilla pudding, Frosted Flakes, and a dollop of honey point the nose in an endlessly appealing direction. On the palate, sugar and spice and everything nice—cinnamon powder and black peppercorn are accompanied by sweeter notes of crème brûlée and French toast topped with powdered sugar. It finishes with just-charred pie crust, gingersnaps, and a lick of orange peel.

n: Talisker The Wild Explorador (Diageo Special Releases 2023), 59.7%
t: Finished in a combination of white, tawny, and ruby port casks. The white port is noticeable first, soaking up the saltiness of seashell-decorated
f: Finished in a combination of white, tawny, and ruby port casks. The white port is noticeable first, soaking up the saltiness of seashell-decorated sandcastles and spices to leave a dry crisp nose, with later floral and fruity notes joining a peaty tang of green herbal and oily fish aromas. Red apple, cherry, cranberry, raspberry, and morello cherry flavors become dry and mouth-drawing before breaking into salted caramel creaminess with banoffee pie and a forceful spicy finish.

n: The ImpEx Collection 15 year old Linkwood 2008, 58.9%
t: This very pale dram drawn from a single hogshead has an opening intensity of five spice aromas, with sliced apple, lemon zest, flaked coconut, peach,
f: This very pale dram drawn from a single hogshead has an opening intensity of five spice aromas, with sliced apple, lemon zest, flaked coconut, peach, and vanilla frosting on the nose. It’s ripe with American oak flavor and a sweet, sugary palate of vanilla fudge, honey, baked lemon, marshmallow, and clove. It’s perfectly approachable without dilution, leaving a lingering finish of zesty lemon, sweet vanilla, and cocoa. (258 bottles)

t: Dried apricot and orange slice give way to caramel sundae syrup, sawdust, ripe cantaloupe, buttered toast with marmalade, and raisin on the nose. The
f: Dried apricot and orange slice give way to caramel sundae syrup, sawdust, ripe cantaloupe, buttered toast with marmalade, and raisin on the nose. The palate carries rich flavors of caramel latte, espresso, dark chocolate, and chocolate fudge, even as a mellow apricot fruitiness remains. More of that lovely dark chocolate and dark roast coffee on the finish, along with dried fruit and chocolate ice cream, will leave you eager for another sip.

n: Preservation Distillery Old Man Winter From the Black Hills (2023), 54.9%
t: At first, the nose is reticent; eventually, notes of Werther’s, caramel macchiato, Whoppers, vanilla fudge, cherry cola, and cream soda arise.
f: At first, the nose is reticent; eventually, notes of Werther’s, caramel macchiato, Whoppers, vanilla fudge, cherry cola, and cream soda arise. This makes the palate somewhat surprising—there’s a barrage of black pepper and deep dark chocolate, as well as tobacco and a whiff of charcoal. A nice roastiness emerges on the finish, with roasted hazelnuts and coffee beans abutted by the darkest of dark chocolate.

n: Ki One Batch 1 Virgin American Oak, 40%
t: A little closed on the nose, but persistence yields citrus peel oils, vanilla, fudge, peppercorn, Brazil nut, and toasted coconut-covered macaroon
f: A little closed on the nose, but persistence yields citrus peel oils, vanilla, fudge, peppercorn, Brazil nut, and toasted coconut-covered macaroon bar. This is sweeter than batch 2 with its first-fill bourbon barrels, and reveals vanilla, lemon tart, orange zest, burnt spices, baked orange, lime, almond, and toffee sweetness. The finish leaves some almond bitterness and slightly acrid burnt spices.

n: Claxton’s Dumbarton 22 year old Bourbon Hogshead, 58.5%
t: Fragrant and floral aromas of lemon meringue pie, jasmine, ripening peach, banana and clementine peel, plus layers of lush citrus and tropical
f: Fragrant and floral aromas of lemon meringue pie, jasmine, ripening peach, banana and clementine peel, plus layers of lush citrus and tropical fruits. It’s pretty nippy at cask strength so water is advisable, but the combination of sweet lemon, vanilla, honey, Starbucks Refreshers, sherbet candy, baked apple, clove, and icing sugar makes this closed-distillery grain whisky a pleasantly sweet sip. (U.S. exclusive; 202 bottles)

t: Accessible scotch blends, like this one from singer Sir Rod Stewart, make perfect introductions to whisky, and this easygoing dram works beautifully
f: Accessible scotch blends, like this one from singer Sir Rod Stewart, make perfect introductions to whisky, and this easygoing dram works beautifully for neat sipping and cocktails. The nose has soft stone fruits, flora notes, sweet vanilla, raspberry, blueberry bubble gum, cinnamon bark, and a hint of oak. It needs a bit more body, but it’s flavorful, with vanilla, baked apple, grated milk chocolate, apricot, baked orange, cinnamon, pepper, and clove.

n: Roseisle 12 year old The Origami Kite (Diageo Special Releases 2023), 56.5%
t: This first single malt release from Roseisle has a nose of orchard and citrus fruit, with kumquat, lime, banana leaf, nectarine, red apple, and
f: This first single malt release from Roseisle has a nose of orchard and citrus fruit, with kumquat, lime, banana leaf, nectarine, red apple, and jasmine, with a touch of white pepper and vanilla oak. Buttery and fruity on the palate, with green apple, orange, lime, and plenty of spice, settling to apple, marshmallow, cotton candy, and background spices. Residual fruit, spice, and a touch of creaminess on the finish.

t: Maighstir, the Gaelic word for “master,” is a collaboration between departing Kentucky Owl master blender John Rhea and his successor,
f: Maighstir, the Gaelic word for “master,” is a collaboration between departing Kentucky Owl master blender John Rhea and his successor, former Diageo blender Maureen Robinson. The nose offers gumdrops, blackberry jam, and spicy herbs, while the palate is soft and fruity, with raisin, sweetened caffe au lait, and some bitter chocolate. Both the palate and the finish are softly textured, and the finish is long and filled with vanilla.

t: This journey starts with a somewhat woody nose, calling to mind sawdust, cedar plank, torched orange, stone fruit, and the faintest whiff of smoke
f: This journey starts with a somewhat woody nose, calling to mind sawdust, cedar plank, torched orange, stone fruit, and the faintest whiff of smoke lingering in the background. On the palate, honey, shortbread cookie, and a sweet sprig of spearmint are joined by more stone fruit and star anise, then juicy slices of white peach and Snapple peach tea come to the fore. The finish is delicate, bursting with stone fruit sweetness and white pepper heat.

n: Elijah Craig Ryder Cup Limited Edition European Toasted Oak Barrel Finished, 47%
t: A pleasantly dry, musty nose calls to mind flipping through the pages of an old book, but it’s livened up by plenty of citrus—namely
f: A pleasantly dry, musty nose calls to mind flipping through the pages of an old book, but it’s livened up by plenty of citrus—namely orange peel and orange-cranberry muffin, maple candies, cinnamon spice oatmeal, and applesauce. Cinnamon takes precedence on the palate, joined by dark chocolate, maple syrup, and a hint of earthiness. The mid-length finish is chock-full of baking chocolate and baking spice, making for an enjoyable experience.

n: Chattanooga Whiskey Vintage Series Bottled in Bond Fall 2019 (Batch 23118F), 50%
t: This smells like the distilled essence of an old-time soda shop. Cherry syrup, chocolate malt, and pistachio ice cream join minty lemonade, a freshly
f: This smells like the distilled essence of an old-time soda shop. Cherry syrup, chocolate malt, and pistachio ice cream join minty lemonade, a freshly mixed Shirley Temple, and vanilla pound cake. On the palate, oak, brownie batter, and egg custard add depth to the soda fountain flavors. This whiskey takes its time on the finish, with espresso, dark chocolate, and brown sugar cinnamon Pop-Tarts.

n: Claxton’s Cameronbridge 30 year old Brandy Quarter Cask, 48.9%
t: Granola bars, sliced apple, honey, mixed peel, cherry, dried fruits, and a touch of chopped herbs on the nose. This is a very enjoyable grain whisky
f: Granola bars, sliced apple, honey, mixed peel, cherry, dried fruits, and a touch of chopped herbs on the nose. This is a very enjoyable grain whisky with a sweet palate of golden syrup, oat bar, dried apricot, citrus peel, warm apple pie, caramel, and walnut. The final phase has some sharp apple notes to keep it lively, with dried fruits, baked pastries, cornflakes, and spice on the finish. (U.S. exclusive; 156 bottles)

n: Old Fitzgerald 10 year old Bottled in Bond (Spring 2023), 50%
t: This bottling of Old Fitz opens with a rich yet balanced nose of pecan pie, cinnamon rolls, and chocolate-hazelnut spread. While the sweets sing
f: This bottling of Old Fitz opens with a rich yet balanced nose of pecan pie, cinnamon rolls, and chocolate-hazelnut spread. While the sweets sing loudest on the nose, the palate brings in base notes of oak, dark chocolate, and tart raspberries and cream. Filling out the harmonious flavors are cherries soaked in brandy, baked apples, and brown sugar. The whiskey feels weighty on the palate and the long finish fades to toasted oak.

t: Plenty of peat up front, along with whiffs of vanilla, citrus, and tobacco before the maritime notes kick in—dried seaweed, sea salt, and
f: Plenty of peat up front, along with whiffs of vanilla, citrus, and tobacco before the maritime notes kick in—dried seaweed, sea salt, and brine. Vanilla and lemon tart on the palate, with light soapiness. It’s delicate, sweet, creamy, and dessert-like. The finish is flavorful with Creamsicle and more vanilla, and the peat reappears. Very balanced overall—not a peat bomb—with subtle sweetness and depth, and peat in a strong but supporting role.

n: Jack Daniel’s Barrel Proof Single Barrel (23-01924), 68.6%
t: Candied notes of dark cherry cough syrup on the nose, with sweet raspberry coulis. It’s a hot one on the palate, with Red Hots, and also offers
f: Candied notes of dark cherry cough syrup on the nose, with sweet raspberry coulis. It’s a hot one on the palate, with Red Hots, and also offers lots of sweetness. It’s similar on the finish, with generous red fruit notes and Atomic Fireball candy. Pleasant, spiced, and lively on the palate and the finish. A high-alcohol bruiser that offers richness and depth along with lip-smacking spice. If spicy ryes are your thing, this one is for you.

t: This 7 year old whiskey is for dessert devotees straight from the jump, as hazelnuts, pound cake, buttercream frosting, strawberry cheesecake,
f: This 7 year old whiskey is for dessert devotees straight from the jump, as hazelnuts, pound cake, buttercream frosting, strawberry cheesecake, blueberry pancakes, maple syrup, and vanilla extract waft from the glass. The palate is wickedly hot, but beneath the initial heat there’s cocoa powder, hot fudge, and cacao nibs. That chocolate remains on the dark and delicious finish, which is long-lasting and has rich notes of Andes chocolates and campfire char.

n: Hirsch The Single Barrel Double Oak (GLD23028), 64%
t: Lots of dried herbs and some baking spice on the nose, milk chocolate and chocolate cake, and brown sugar as it settles down to become softer.
f: Lots of dried herbs and some baking spice on the nose, milk chocolate and chocolate cake, and brown sugar as it settles down to become softer. Sweetness of black cherry soda and more chocolate on the palate. A big one that’s a bit hot, but it eases nicely with water, bringing notes of warm chocolate brownies. Long and spiced on the finish, with marshmallow and chocolate.

t: Baker’s has been an impressive pour since its relaunch in 2019 as a single barrel bourbon but this older, limited release pushes the label to
f: Baker’s has been an impressive pour since its relaunch in 2019 as a single barrel bourbon but this older, limited release pushes the label to new heights. Rich and decadent in every facet, it opens with peanut brittle, pecan pie, and baked apples dredged in brown sugar. There’s oak and a bit of barrel char, but those drier notes sing harmony to the nutty lead. Water brings out apple turnovers and banana pudding, while the finish adds a bristly kick of cinnamon spice.

n: Royal Salute 21 year old The Jodhpur Edition, 40%
t: A virgin oak finish helps conjure up the spirit of Jodhpur, India, the birthplace of modern polo, with a nose that transports you to the spice market
f: A virgin oak finish helps conjure up the spirit of Jodhpur, India, the birthplace of modern polo, with a nose that transports you to the spice market with heady aromas of turmeric, cumin, cardamom, clove, sea salt, mixed peel, and pencil shavings. Light on the palate, with citrus and summer berries, then robust pepperiness with clove, cinnamon, and toasted oak before concluding with flavors of brown sugar and Whoppers.

n: Pinhook 7 year old Vertical Series Tiz Rye Time, 52.56%
t: The fourth of 12 planned releases in Pinhook’s Vertical Series, Tiz Rye admirably balances elegance and power. The nose is somewhat restrained,
f: The fourth of 12 planned releases in Pinhook’s Vertical Series, Tiz Rye admirably balances elegance and power. The nose is somewhat restrained, with dark chocolate and sweet spearmint blending like an Andes mint before getting punchier on the palate. Oak, barrel char, cinnamon-raisin bread, and spiced apples are packed into every sip, with each layer vying to come out on top. The finish amps up the herbal quality and brings in a numbing note, akin to Sichuan peppercorns.

t: Sugary sweet, the nose opens over a tray of freshly baked sugar cookies, vanilla frosting, cherry-dipped vanilla soft serve, and coffee creamer. Such
f: Sugary sweet, the nose opens over a tray of freshly baked sugar cookies, vanilla frosting, cherry-dipped vanilla soft serve, and coffee creamer. Such confection delights follow through to the palate, though more grounded notes of ripe cherry and cinnamon stick give the dram some heft. The finish is hot and spicy, offering up a big kick of Big Red gum, and it goes funky at the tail end with a burst of mustard seed. An unexpected and engaging trip.

t: There’s sugar and spice on the nose: there’s cinnamon stick, gingersnaps, gingerbread, rum cake, Necco wafers, and a zesty zing from
f: There’s sugar and spice on the nose: there’s cinnamon stick, gingersnaps, gingerbread, rum cake, Necco wafers, and a zesty zing from fresh orange slices. Red Hots coat the mouth, though once the heat subsides there are gentler flavors of warm cinnamon babka and Cinnamon Roll ice cream. More of that cinnamon spice on the finish, which leads with lightly burnt cinnamon sugar toast.

t: A mild, mellow dram, with fudge, background smoke, orange peel, florals, white pepper, and ground almond. It’s smooth on the palate, with
f: A mild, mellow dram, with fudge, background smoke, orange peel, florals, white pepper, and ground almond. It’s smooth on the palate, with honey, clementine, light smoke, fudge, pepperiness, then some stale chocolate bars, chestnut, and praline as the smoke builds up toward a climax of dark chocolate, licorice, and pepper. The interplay between the smoke and praline flavors works particularly well, but it’s the most tranquil blend in the range.

t: This is a chocolate box of delights. Kept aloft by aromas of honey, vanilla, and candied orange, with barley and flora scents, it adds tangy dried
f: This is a chocolate box of delights. Kept aloft by aromas of honey, vanilla, and candied orange, with barley and flora scents, it adds tangy dried apricots, mango, hazelnut, and gentle spices. Creamy chocolate on the palate, with leather, peppercorn, clove, and licorice, then flavors of creamy caramel, nuts, and cortado lighten the mood before a long, deep finish of chocolate, coffee, and exotic spices.

n: Bushwood Black Label Stillwater Single Barrel (Batch 1), 47.5%
t: Bushwood’s first release of Stillwater rye leads with a generous nose of French toast, maple syrup, brown sugar, and a hint of baking rye
f: Bushwood’s first release of Stillwater rye leads with a generous nose of French toast, maple syrup, brown sugar, and a hint of baking rye bread. This rye is corn-heavy, with a mashbill of 51% rye, 45% corn, and 4% malted barley, and the caramel corn, vanilla, and chocolate orange notes on the palate reflect the grains’ influence. As the sip develops, anise, caraway, and tart apple cider emerge. The finish is peppery and chocolaty, fading evenly.

n: Proof and Wood 21 year old Good & Sunshine Jamaican Rum Barrel Finished, 52.5%
t: A nice kick of baking spice leads the nose, followed by cinnamon raisin toast, a dollop of honey, and pleasant maltiness. There’s bright citrus
f: A nice kick of baking spice leads the nose, followed by cinnamon raisin toast, a dollop of honey, and pleasant maltiness. There’s bright citrus by way of orange peel too, plus a whiff of vanilla bean. The palate hews spicy—Red Hots take center stage, joined by a crack of white pepper. The rum cask presents a fruity mustiness that adds an interesting twist. More cinnamon heat, honey, and some chocolate malt on the finish, which lingers on for quite a while.

t: Returning after a long absence, the new 10 year old has zested lemon, vanilla, lemongrass, and robust peatiness, with a touch of minerality shaping
f: Returning after a long absence, the new 10 year old has zested lemon, vanilla, lemongrass, and robust peatiness, with a touch of minerality shaping the crispness and purity of the aromas. It’s fruit-forward with banana and green apple among honey, vanilla, butteriness, and egg custard, with a long-lasting spiciness of pepper, clove, and a hint of brine. A growing oakiness with salted caramel, pepper, and fruit to finish.

n: Whiskey Del Bac Frontera (2023 Limited Edition), 48.5%
t: Lovely aromas of wood spice and torched orange are swiftly joined by pound cake, sugar cookie, vanilla bean, and a hint of must. The palate is just
f: Lovely aromas of wood spice and torched orange are swiftly joined by pound cake, sugar cookie, vanilla bean, and a hint of must. The palate is just as beguiling, sprinkled with delicately sweet notes of yellow cupcake, buttercream frosting, and dulce de leche, and later, bursts of cherry pie, toasted almonds, and caramel syrup. Lemon peel on the finish, as well as dark roast coffee with turbinado sugar.

t: This elegant French single malt is floral, subtle, and a joy to sip. The nose gracefully rises from the glass with potpourri, apple juice, and
f: This elegant French single malt is floral, subtle, and a joy to sip. The nose gracefully rises from the glass with potpourri, apple juice, and honeyed grains. Throughout the nose there’s a subtle hint of oak and vanilla sweetness. The palate turns fruiter, with tropical pineapple and mango interleaved with apples and pears. The oak is extremely subdued with each sip, presenting as a mild toasted bitterness and over-steeped tea. The finish is soft and light with mild oakiness.

t: Lebanese single malt produced by Riachi Distillery. Licorice, dried vine fruit, cigar wrapper, nutmeg, root beer, unsweetened chocolate, and aromas
f: Lebanese single malt produced by Riachi Distillery. Licorice, dried vine fruit, cigar wrapper, nutmeg, root beer, unsweetened chocolate, and aromas of dry, woody cask extractives, so let it breathe a while. Chocolate, sweet baked orange, and pepper as the alcohol peaks, then honey, nut butter, and maple syrup. A root beer bitterness develops, with licorice, oak astringency, and sour woody flavors, with a finish of aniseed and cough syrup. Cedar and new oak make for an overpowering combination. (241 bottles)

n: Lost Lantern Soaring Spice Frey Ranch Distillery Nevada Straight Bourbon, 63.8%
t: Orange peel, fresh grain, dried herbs and spices, fiery spice on the nose, and light fruit notes emerge with water. Very spiced on the palate, with
f: Orange peel, fresh grain, dried herbs and spices, fiery spice on the nose, and light fruit notes emerge with water. Very spiced on the palate, with more dried orange and dried raspberry and cherry notes. Much softer with water, but still with a very dry restrained sort of balance that is spicy, earthy, and enjoyable. The finish is the best part, with candied sweetness and vanilla melding well with the spice for a happy ending.

t: The nose offers sweet notes of raspberry Italian ice, ripe grapes, sweetened iced tea, cinnamon cake, and melted butterscotch, balanced against a
f: The nose offers sweet notes of raspberry Italian ice, ripe grapes, sweetened iced tea, cinnamon cake, and melted butterscotch, balanced against a light antique shop earthiness and spiced oak. Spicy and hot on the palate, accented with chile peppers, and offering fresh coffee grounds, bitter chocolate, dried cherries, and dried orange slices, leading to a finish of vanilla, almond, and perfumed oak. A dry flavor profile overall, with the barrel influence leading.

t: Sea salt and a pleasant maritime tang start off on the nose, as this Newport, Rhode Island distiller displays its seaside origins. There are also
f: Sea salt and a pleasant maritime tang start off on the nose, as this Newport, Rhode Island distiller displays its seaside origins. There are also hints of lilac and grape hard candy on this very fragrant nose. The palate is polished and well-integrated, with bright citrus and hints of malt, vanilla, and balanced oak. ABV is just 45%, but add water and the flavors expand even more, providing some very pleasant sipping.

t: This year’s blend of single pot still and single malt whiskeys is full-bodied, flavorful, and confidently quaffable at cask strength.
f: This year’s blend of single pot still and single malt whiskeys is full-bodied, flavorful, and confidently quaffable at cask strength. There’s plenty of American oak cask character to explore on the nose, with caramel, malt, vanilla, toffee, and hazelnut, balanced with ground pepper, candied ginger, and dried citrus. There’s no real urgency to add water; just soak up the flavors of baked orange, toffee, ginger, and pepper.

n: High N’ Wicked 5 year old High Rye Cask Strength, 62.6%
t: Fruity and dense, the nose has plenty to love: there’s Fig Newton, fruit-and-nut roll, fresh apple slices, Martinelli’s apple juice, and
f: Fruity and dense, the nose has plenty to love: there’s Fig Newton, fruit-and-nut roll, fresh apple slices, Martinelli’s apple juice, and cherry cough drop. Cinnamon and apples overtake the palate, with caramel apple, baked apple, and cinnamon stick front and center. A decent amount of char and wood are also present, and the char in particular picks up on the finish, partnered with caramel swirl, coffee bean, and apple muffin.

t: Overripe fruit, assertive rum esters, and chocolate-covered raisins lead on this confident single malt’s nose. Once the almost fermented notes
f: Overripe fruit, assertive rum esters, and chocolate-covered raisins lead on this confident single malt’s nose. Once the almost fermented notes have been navigated, the whisky shows softer cinnamon roll aromas, with toffee and butterscotch. The palate tamps down the overripe notes, gracefully softening into dried berries, orange oil, and French toast. The finish is raisin and candied pecan-forward, fading over a moderate length of time.

t: Matured in oloroso, PX, and red wine casks, this whisky’s nose is rich and luxuriant with mixed peels, raisin, Christmas pudding, fig roll,
f: Matured in oloroso, PX, and red wine casks, this whisky’s nose is rich and luxuriant with mixed peels, raisin, Christmas pudding, fig roll, fine spices, and notable high-alcohol strength. The casks work their magic, producing a palate of baked orange, dates, currants, strawberry, light toffee, clove, and pepper, drifting off dreamily into a land of lemon curd, creamy fudge, and melting white chocolate.

t: Initially, there are dark sherry notes of plum, black cherry, and soy sauce, with a lift of gentle spices, then it evolves, adding caramel- ized
f: Initially, there are dark sherry notes of plum, black cherry, and soy sauce, with a lift of gentle spices, then it evolves, adding caramel- ized roasted garlic, lemongrass, ginger, and concentrated notes of aged balsamic vinegar. A burst of browned butter on the palate, followed by nutty flavors, with ripe plum, damson, a dash of balsamic, clove, pepper, melted chocolate, and a mouth-filling finish of powdery cocoa.

n: Glenmorangie A Tale of The Forest, 46%
t: Barbecue lovers will find refuge in this whisky, which smells like a Fourth of July party—there are burnt ends, mesquite smoke, charcoal grill,
f: Barbecue lovers will find refuge in this whisky, which smells like a Fourth of July party—there are burnt ends, mesquite smoke, charcoal grill, brisket, and grilled corn husks. A hint of strawberry sweetness balances out these meaty, smoky flavors. The palate is surprisingly fruity, with strong notes of raspberry coulis, ripe red berries, and orange scone. Long-lasting spice, cooling menthol, and rooibos tea on the finish complete this winding, mouthwatering journey.  No.-8 Top 20 2023

t: For each batch, Wemyss’s signature peated Islay malt is married with a supporting cast of base malts for 8 weeks. Lightly floral on the nose,
f: For each batch, Wemyss’s signature peated Islay malt is married with a supporting cast of base malts for 8 weeks. Lightly floral on the nose, with vanilla, citrus, peppery spice, coastal notes, and beach barbecue smoke. This has plenty of body and makes for a good fireside sipper, with flavors of citrus, vanilla, peat smoke, and light toffee, with a slight salinity, finishing with pepper, clove, and chocolate.

t: Lapsang souchong, tarry ropes, hot tires on asphalt, red chile, and peppermint—the smoke is in charge here. This is perfectly drinkable at cask
f: Lapsang souchong, tarry ropes, hot tires on asphalt, red chile, and peppermint—the smoke is in charge here. This is perfectly drinkable at cask strength, with an initial burst of red fruit flavors, cherry, plum, damson, and fig, backed with chocolate and peppery spice. As the pepperiness releases its grip, there’s tobacco, coffee bean, nutmeg, and leather, with toasted oak and cacao on a long spicy finish.

t: The flagship Dingle is just a great whiskey to lose yourself in. The nose has honey on wheat toast, brown sugar, orange, lime, malt, dried fruit,
f: The flagship Dingle is just a great whiskey to lose yourself in. The nose has honey on wheat toast, brown sugar, orange, lime, malt, dried fruit, golden sultana, and gentle oak spices. It tastes of cinnamon breakfast cereal, golden syrup, toast, vanilla, and peppercorn, with creamy malt, hazelnut, toffee, and dried fruits as it opens up. A smooth finish with cinnamon, nutmeg, and a hint of espresso.

t: This bold, flavorsome single malt was matured in PX sherry casks with a portion finished in casks seasoned with exotic Indian botanicals;
f: This bold, flavorsome single malt was matured in PX sherry casks with a portion finished in casks seasoned with exotic Indian botanicals; temperatures in the warehouse can reach 100°F. Bold, intense aromas of figs, currants, cola, Garibaldi biscuits, treacle, oak extrac- tives, and fragrant spices with a little heat, then the palate follows through with prune, fig, sultana, black cherry, licorice, pepper, brown sugar, malt, and leather. Excellent over ice.

t: Matured in bourbon and sherry casks, this marries aromas of sweet vanilla, apricot, and sooty peat smoke with dry notes of dark wood, leather,
f: Matured in bourbon and sherry casks, this marries aromas of sweet vanilla, apricot, and sooty peat smoke with dry notes of dark wood, leather, chocolate, dried seaweed, and ground pepper. This is definitely one for those who prefer sweeter whiskies, with honeyed fresh orchard fruit, rum-and-raisin fudge, sherry, golden syrup, and supportive spices that endure as the sweetness fades in the finish.

t: With PX sherry and marsala cask influences, this seamlessly exudes the quality of its single pot still character throughout. The nose balances light
f: With PX sherry and marsala cask influences, this seamlessly exudes the quality of its single pot still character throughout. The nose balances light fruits with fine spices, showing orange cake, glacé cherry, finely ground pepper, crisp red apple, and some barley sweetness. A thick mouthfeel, with marmalade, pot still spices, toffee, cinnamon, clove, and pepper, then easing off the spice to serve up stewed apple, chocolate shavings, and plum.

n: Boulder Spirits The Trailhead 4.5 year old, 52.5%
t: Oak, sweetness, spice, and fresh hay notes on the nose are enjoyable, with the oak slightly out in front. Medium bodied on the palate, with some
f: Oak, sweetness, spice, and fresh hay notes on the nose are enjoyable, with the oak slightly out in front. Medium bodied on the palate, with some green and youthful spirits notes couple with candy store flavors of circus peanuts and banana taffy that meet earthy oak and tobacco on the medium finish.

t: This Speyside-led blended malt has a charming nose of honey, vanilla sponge cake, marzipan, floral notes, oak shavings, and tangerine. Light citrus
f: This Speyside-led blended malt has a charming nose of honey, vanilla sponge cake, marzipan, floral notes, oak shavings, and tangerine. Light citrus on the palate, with a silken-honeyed mouthfeel; there’s vanilla fudge, pepper, beeswax, spice, candied orange, and long-lasting peppery notes, with tangy citrus coming through in the end. The finish is strong and lengthy, with spices riding the coattails of the sweet honey, orange, and lemon.

n: Hard Truth Master Distiller’s Reserve Caramel Malt Barrel Strength Sweet Mash (Batch 001), 58.7%
t: This rye adds in 11% caramel malted barley to a more traditional mash of 51% rye and 38% corn, playing with both the typical and the experimental.
f: This rye adds in 11% caramel malted barley to a more traditional mash of 51% rye and 38% corn, playing with both the typical and the experimental. The nose offers a fruit salad’s worth of aromas: apples, pears, tangerines, orange peel, and tropical fruits like pineapple and kiwi. The sip spices the fruits with cinnamon raisin bread, apple cider doughnuts, and mulled wine. The finish wraps up with caramel-drizzled whipped cream over coffee

t: A subtle and sweet nose delivers lemon icing, banana pudding with Nilla wafers, glazed doughnut, vanilla pound cake, and peanut brittle. With
f: A subtle and sweet nose delivers lemon icing, banana pudding with Nilla wafers, glazed doughnut, vanilla pound cake, and peanut brittle. With water, the nose turns doughy, like fresh-baked challah, with hints of pine. On the palate, vanilla cream, blueberry muffin, and yogurt-covered pretzel. The texture is lush and velvety. Grape candies, more pine, cracked black pepper, and bitter lemon accentuate the finish. Solid and consistent, if a touch hot. (6,391 bottles)

t: This smells like a dessert treat, with a nose that’s all banana split and sweet mint. Whipped cream, banana, and caramel syrup vie with an
f: This smells like a dessert treat, with a nose that’s all banana split and sweet mint. Whipped cream, banana, and caramel syrup vie with an herbal underbrush of pine forest, dried leaves, and anise. It has excellent body and delivers fresh fruit, with pears, berries sparring with licorice, and an ever-present mintiness on the palate. The finish is peppery and drier—quite different from the sip—and lasts and lasts.

t: Expressive and wood-forward on the nose, with honeyed granola, blueberry yogurt, baked apple, fresh-cut lumber, and candied orange. There’s a
f: Expressive and wood-forward on the nose, with honeyed granola, blueberry yogurt, baked apple, fresh-cut lumber, and candied orange. There’s a creamy vanilla note with that woodiness—like eating ice cream with a wooden spoon—that carries over to the palate, where shaved coconut, candied pineapple, and salted crackers are found. Big spice, roast coffee, and bitter chocolate highlight the finish. Verges on too youthful and hot at times but charms otherwise.

n: Widow Jane 14 year old The Vaults 2022 (Batch 1), 49.5%
t: Jars of dark berry jam open on the nose, blackberry and raspberry at the fore. Sticking with breakfast, there are also glazed doughnuts and maple
f: Jars of dark berry jam open on the nose, blackberry and raspberry at the fore. Sticking with breakfast, there are also glazed doughnuts and maple syrup on pancakes, as well as a drop of vanilla extract and a sprinkle of espresso powder. There are soft, sweet flavors on the palate as well, like milk chocolate and vanilla custard, but also an accompanying bright burst of red fruit and a dash of black pepper. Water coaxes that pepper out even more, but it’s married beautifully with vanilla sweetness.

n: Cask 88 The Book of Demonologie 13 year old (Cask No. 26), 52%
t: Part of the Scottish Witchcraft Series, this 2009 cask hails from a secret Orkney distillery. It stirs with a nose of cherry lips candy, peat smoke,
f: Part of the Scottish Witchcraft Series, this 2009 cask hails from a secret Orkney distillery. It stirs with a nose of cherry lips candy, peat smoke, salty sea air, toasted teacake, lime Jell-O, and lavender bath salts. Warm sherry notes with fruitcake flavors of cherry, mixed peel, walnut, and vine fruit, then a peppery peak before becoming syrupy with honey, lemon zest, dark toffee, date, and fig on the other side. (online exclusive, £98; 165 bottles)

n: Carpathian Romanian Wine Cask Collection Pinot Noir Cask, 46%
t: An attractive nose of summer fruits on first impression, with aromas of strawberry, red currant, floral bouquets, vanilla cream, and white pepper.
f: An attractive nose of summer fruits on first impression, with aromas of strawberry, red currant, floral bouquets, vanilla cream, and white pepper. There’s a lovely subtleness to the Romanian pinot noir wine-cask maturation here, showing heather honey and red currant flavors, plus some hot pepper, then caramel, vanilla, dried fruit, damson, and toffee as the spices settle down and the flavors round out.

n: Shizuoka Pot Still W 100% Imported Barley First Edition Duo Set, 55.5%
t: Tart citrus acidity on the nose, with clementine peel oils, lime jelly, fleshy grapefruit, but also rose petals and cotton candy sweetness.
f: Tart citrus acidity on the nose, with clementine peel oils, lime jelly, fleshy grapefruit, but also rose petals and cotton candy sweetness. It’s ridiculously delicious, though it offers less complexity than its Pot Still K counterpart in the set, encapsulating a combination of caramel, malt, citrus peel, crushed peppercorn, and clove, diluting to reveal almond nougat, toffee, and walnut. A hot dry finish of crushed nuts and dark chocolate. (250 sets of 200-ml bottles for the U.S.)

n: Redwood Empire Cask Strength Emerald Giant 2022 (Batch 001), 58.2%
t: There’s a savory, herbaceous quality to the nose, calling to mind tea leaves, dried herbs, and a sprig of mint. Sweeter notes, like Andes
f: There’s a savory, herbaceous quality to the nose, calling to mind tea leaves, dried herbs, and a sprig of mint. Sweeter notes, like Andes chocolates, vanilla frosting, and yellow cake soon join the mix, creating a lovely balance between honeyed and herb-driven notes. The palate takes that sweetness and spice even further—there’s delicious heat on the tip of the tongue, giving way to raspberry-filled chocolate squares, black forest cake, and ripe red fruit. The finish amps up the dark chocolate, with a kiss of berry fruit at the end.

t: This was my second lowest rated whiskey from the 2009 Collection (a 91 rating). This one is an impressive whiskey, and an improvement from last year.
f: This was my second lowest rated whiskey from the 2009 Collection (a 91 rating). This one is an impressive whiskey, and an improvement from last year. It’s soft (for a straight rye), well rounded, and easy to embrace, with tamed spice (cinnamon, mint, vanilla, mocha), nougat, toffee, fruit (bramble, subtle citrus), subtle date, and polished leather on the finish. Buffalo Trace is playing a shell game with this aged rye (being stored in stainless steel tanks over the past several years until new stocks mature), but in this instance there seems to be a prize under every shell. Well done! (Editor's Choice)

t: This is a barrel-stave finished whiskey that brings together staves from bourbon barrels, new French oak, and sherry casks to create a crisp and
f: This is a barrel-stave finished whiskey that brings together staves from bourbon barrels, new French oak, and sherry casks to create a crisp and tropical rye, complete with crackling baking spice and rich stewed fruits. The nose opens with grapefruit, pineapple, mango sorbet, and Creamsicle. The palate cooks the fruit, introducing jammy sweetness, peach melba, and toasted baking spices. The finish dries out and ends with chocolate-covered espresso beans.

n: Bardstown Bourbon Company Chateau De Laubade Armagnac Cask Finished (2022 Release), 53.5%
t: The nose is subtle and seductive; cream soda, angel food cake, tobacco leaves, candied orange, and an earthy hint of old leather. There is a lot to
f: The nose is subtle and seductive; cream soda, angel food cake, tobacco leaves, candied orange, and an earthy hint of old leather. There is a lot to unpack, all of it skillfully arranged. On the palate, almond and vanilla, Ferrero Rocher, green apple, chocolate-covered cherries, raspberry jam, and cinnamon French toast. The finish is dry and fruity, with cocoa powder and vanilla icing. A beautiful union of spirit and finishing cask. Artfully made.

t: Blackberry jam, blueberry pancakes, new leather, and tobacco leaf on the nose. Powerful on the palate, with an opening blast of cinnamon followed by
f: Blackberry jam, blueberry pancakes, new leather, and tobacco leaf on the nose. Powerful on the palate, with an opening blast of cinnamon followed by strawberry jam, dried herbs, dark chocolate, espresso, and vanilla flan. Drinking it with a big rock of ice is recommended. Excellent length on the finish, with more jammy fruitiness, cinnamon bun, and dark chocolate. It’s a brawny whiskey that carries its proof with great structure, balance, and complexity.

t: Fruity and tart on the nose, with aromas of strawberry lemonade, cinnamon-dusted apples, watermelon candy, and musty oak. A rich, syrupy palate
f: Fruity and tart on the nose, with aromas of strawberry lemonade, cinnamon-dusted apples, watermelon candy, and musty oak. A rich, syrupy palate brings with it notes of strawberry frosting, bubble gum, raisin pudding, and vanilla. A dessert sweetness takes the foreground while cherry and raspberry notes fill in the margins. The finish is creamy, with more red berries and vanilla. It’s young but shows promise.

n: Shinobu Pure Malt Mizunara Oak Finish, 43%
t: The inviting nose has heather honey, beeswax, vanilla sponge, green apple, pear, grapefruit, white pepper, and notes of exotic woods. This blend has
f: The inviting nose has heather honey, beeswax, vanilla sponge, green apple, pear, grapefruit, white pepper, and notes of exotic woods. This blend has excellent balance: The mizunara exerts influence without dominating the nose. The palate has light yellow fruits, lemon, creamy fudge, pepper, fruit tarts, grapefruit, and a finish of nutmeg, cinnamon, and milky coffee.

n: Red Line Toasted New Oak Barrel Finished Single Barrel (No. TR118), 57%
t: This rustic rye hits hard with a punchy nose of dried cinnamon, pithy orange peel, and lemon zest. The palate surges with a big wave of flavor
f: This rustic rye hits hard with a punchy nose of dried cinnamon, pithy orange peel, and lemon zest. The palate surges with a big wave of flavor leading with new wood, high-cacao dark chocolate, chocolate oranges, vanilla bean, and a pronounced pepperiness. The finish skids into more new oak, dark chocolate, and vanilla. Overall this is a bold pour that hits hard, even after adding water.

t: Notes of fresh lemon, chocolate, and candied orange slices emerge on the nose, while the palate is deliciously rich, creamy, and smooth, with
f: Notes of fresh lemon, chocolate, and candied orange slices emerge on the nose, while the palate is deliciously rich, creamy, and smooth, with balanced spice and a pleasant texture. It definitely benefits from water, which unlocks more sweet orange, spice, and seasoned oak. The rich finish offers a crescendo of espresso and tart black pepper melding with dark chocolate and a hint of orange peel. A complex whiskey with lots to enjoy.

t: Matured in sherry, bourbon, and American white oak casks, this is delicately scented with plum, cherry, black currant, floral notes, gentle honey
f: Matured in sherry, bourbon, and American white oak casks, this is delicately scented with plum, cherry, black currant, floral notes, gentle honey sweetness, pepper, and clove. It retains that dewy grass note of rice whiskies. Ripe plum, mouth-drying in the grip of the oak tannins, then leather, baked sugar, stewed fruits, fig, baking spices, and some sticky sherry notes, with fruit skins and peppery spices on the finish.

n: Penderyn 6 year old Rye Single Cask 685/2016, 60.7%
t: A sweet, floral, and spicy nose with aromas of shortbread, lemon sorbet, vanilla sponge, poached pear, cinnamon, nutmeg, green banana, ground ginger,
f: A sweet, floral, and spicy nose with aromas of shortbread, lemon sorbet, vanilla sponge, poached pear, cinnamon, nutmeg, green banana, ground ginger, and dried apple. Lime, lemon, vanilla sweetness, butterscotch, candy corn, pepper, and ginger root flavors, with the spices riding high on the cask strength alcohol, falling back to toasted nuts, peanut brittle, rye spices, griddled brioche, and oak. Try a little water to make it even spicier. (219, bottles, U.S. exclusive)

n: Four Roses Limited Edition Small Batch (2022 Release), 54.5%
t: The nose is complex, offering up oak, ripe red cherries, and cherry pie alongside more herbaceous notes like cloves and leather. The palate is smooth
f: The nose is complex, offering up oak, ripe red cherries, and cherry pie alongside more herbaceous notes like cloves and leather. The palate is smooth and creamy, and while there are still cherries present, hot cinnamon spice and cayenne pepper-infused dark chocolate also appear. The cinnamon isn’t overpowering; it’s tempered nicely by vanilla soft serve and, toward the end, fresh mint. The finish is the figurative cherry on top, lengthy and striking a solid balance of vanilla sweetness with spice. (14,100 bottles)

n: Hotel Tango 6 year old American Straight Reserver, 45%
t: This is a funky one. Yeast fills the nose, calling to mind freshly baked bread, hay, and a musty old barn, though there’s a pleasant honey-on
f: This is a funky one. Yeast fills the nose, calling to mind freshly baked bread, hay, and a musty old barn, though there’s a pleasant honey-on toast aroma, too. The palate is light and a bit thin, and tends toward sugary flavors like powdered sugar, creme brûlée, and candied lemon. Cinnamon spice yields the faintest heat, though it fades quickly. A short finish takes this one home, and it follows the path shown on the palate by way of vanilla extract and lemon.

n: The Singleton of Glen Ord 15 year old (Diageo Special Releases 2022), 54.2%
t: Red apple, cranberry, damson, and ground pepper on first sniff, this showcases a beautifully layered bouquet of wood spices, caramel, cream, and more
f: Red apple, cranberry, damson, and ground pepper on first sniff, this showcases a beautifully layered bouquet of wood spices, caramel, cream, and more overt vinous aromas. The palate begins with warm baked fruits, watermelon, crystalized sugar, clove, pepper, Red Vines, red apple, taffy, and fruity red wine before a spicy finish. The cautious addition of a little water opens it up fully.

t: Produced at Mars Shinshu Distillery and aged in bourbon, port, and sherry casks, this has a nose of pepper, ground ginger, cumin, sea salt, black
f: Produced at Mars Shinshu Distillery and aged in bourbon, port, and sherry casks, this has a nose of pepper, ground ginger, cumin, sea salt, black olive tapenade, mushroom duxelle, fruit teas, and banana chews. With flavors of honey, almond fruitcake, orange zest, pepper, and clove, it retains the citrus sweetness throughout a long spicy phase, ending with dried cranberry, oak, persimmon, and bitter Seville orange peel in marmalade. (5,374 bottles)

t: Made with nearly 50% wheat. The nose is all butterscotch, caramel, and vanilla, creating a sweet core for layers of cherry cola, Earl Grey tea, and
f: Made with nearly 50% wheat. The nose is all butterscotch, caramel, and vanilla, creating a sweet core for layers of cherry cola, Earl Grey tea, and citrus candies to rest. The palate is dense with sweet desserts, berry compote, chocolate-covered raisins, and a balancing cayenne spice. The finish is long and spicy and the high proof allows the flavors, especially the pepper spice, to pleasantly linger.

n: Cameron Bridge 26 year old (Diageo Special Releases 2022), 56.2%
t: Matured in refill American oak, the nose has honey on hot porridge, peppercorn, cinnamon, nutmeg, brown sugar, green foliage, and hints of toffee. At
f: Matured in refill American oak, the nose has honey on hot porridge, peppercorn, cinnamon, nutmeg, brown sugar, green foliage, and hints of toffee. At full strength there is orange peel, grapefruit, pepper, red apple, and fiery spices, followed by pomegranate and cherry Life Savers, with more measured fruitiness as the spices ebb away. Although the grain distillery is named Cameronbridge, the expression’s name acknowledges past bottlings like Cameron Brig.

n: Red Line 6 year old Cask Strength Single Barrel (No. 155), 56.5%
t: Dessert lovers, rejoice: This is made for you. The nose is redolent of Rolos, Milk Duds, cocoa powder, hot fudge, and Raisinets. These carry on to
f: Dessert lovers, rejoice: This is made for you. The nose is redolent of Rolos, Milk Duds, cocoa powder, hot fudge, and Raisinets. These carry on to the creamy palate, where rich hot cocoa and dark chocolate-covered espresso beans are supplemented by just the right amount of heat from cinnamon spice and ginger. A lovely zip of red fruit bursts forth on the finish, which lingers on and on, making for a gift that keeps on giving.—JH

t: White grape, sea salt, sliced pear, and admirable maritime aromas of rock pools and dried seaweed, with a hint of new plasticine and wood spice.
f: White grape, sea salt, sliced pear, and admirable maritime aromas of rock pools and dried seaweed, with a hint of new plasticine and wood spice. Sweet and thick on the tongue, with honey, lemon and lime marmalade, pepper, and chile flakes as the wave of alcohol breaks, leaving lemon meringue pie, fruit compote, and a late return of that coastal saltiness. Best enjoyed at cask strength, so avoid the water.

n: Oban The Distillers Edition (Distilled in 2007/Bottled in 2021), 43%
t: Fragrant stone fruits fill the nose: sliced white peaches, canned peaches, and apricots. Stay awhile, and earthier notes of sweet peat, fresh
f: Fragrant stone fruits fill the nose: sliced white peaches, canned peaches, and apricots. Stay awhile, and earthier notes of sweet peat, fresh flowers, and cedar plank emerge. The palate is smooth, and though it’s light there is an incredible creamy texture that’s furthered by candied orange, applesauce, and warm apple crisp. The finish has divine depth, and is rich with vanilla frozen custard and more of those initial stone fruit flavors.

t: Smoked ham on the bone, brine, highly aromatic smoke, and toasted oak, with the spices in a supportive role. Despite being more punchy and smoky than
f: Smoked ham on the bone, brine, highly aromatic smoke, and toasted oak, with the spices in a supportive role. Despite being more punchy and smoky than the 2021 release, there’s superb balance on the nose here. The palate opens with sweet vanilla, cotton candy, baked ham slathered in molasses, powerful spices, lemon peel, and red chile flakes, with peppery smoke on a lengthy finish.

n: Koshi-No Shinobu Pure Malt Lightly Peated 10 year old Mizunara Oak Finish, 43%
t: Give this a little time and space, as the rich aromatic mizunara notes lie tantalizingly beyond the garden bonfire smoke; then there’s
f: Give this a little time and space, as the rich aromatic mizunara notes lie tantalizingly beyond the garden bonfire smoke; then there’s licorice, heather honey, deep wood notes, and chocolate hobnobs. A flavorsome blend with a trajectory that spans iced coffee, malt, pepper, runny caramel, clove, chocolate milkshake, oak char, melting chocolate bombs, and peppery smoke.

t: Matured for nearly 7 years in bourbon and scotch casks, think of this like a spicy red apple dipped in chocolate. On the nose, there’s fresh
f: Matured for nearly 7 years in bourbon and scotch casks, think of this like a spicy red apple dipped in chocolate. On the nose, there’s fresh red apple, red cherry, watermelon, syrup, peppercorn, clove, salted caramel, and licorice. The flavors begin with plum, red apple, and mandarin, then spiced chocolate, a hint of smoke, coffee, chocolate cake, black cherry, Brazil nut, dark vanilla, and a spicy peppery finish. (3,900 bottles; 210 bottles for U.S.)

n: Old Elk Master’s Blend Series Double Wheat, 53.55%
t: A blend of wheat whiskey and wheated bourbon. Fruity, sweet, and grain-forward on the nose, with strawberry hard candies, honey-wheat pretzels,
f: A blend of wheat whiskey and wheated bourbon. Fruity, sweet, and grain-forward on the nose, with strawberry hard candies, honey-wheat pretzels, graham crackers, and lemon meringue pie. With water, peanut brittle and tiramisu. There’s additional honey then bread on the palate, along with peppery spice, burnt brown sugar, espresso beans, and bitter chocolate. That spice and chocolate carry over to the finish, which evokes nutty chocolate brownies. A rich and flavorful whiskey that benefits from a few drops of water.

n: ImpEx Collection (distilled at Penderyn) 5 year old Blandy’s Malvasia Madeira Cask, 57.4%
t: This vibrant single cask whisky has an attractive nose of dried cherry, prune, currants, raisin, rosehip, furniture polish, and stewed apples.
f: This vibrant single cask whisky has an attractive nose of dried cherry, prune, currants, raisin, rosehip, furniture polish, and stewed apples. It’s a dry, sweet, full-bodied whisky, with apple syrup, strawberry, damson, caramel, and creamy toffee, the alcohol rising steadily to crest with pepper, bathing the taste buds with comforting waves of sweet fruits, red currant, and rose hip. A rather spectacular whisky. (486 bottles)

t: Head distiller and blender Donal Farrell finished this whiskey in IPA casks, confirmed by the zested orange, candied lemon, and bitterness on the
f: Head distiller and blender Donal Farrell finished this whiskey in IPA casks, confirmed by the zested orange, candied lemon, and bitterness on the nose. Add to that some aromas of honey, ground almond, dried grasses, whipped cream, and a grating of nutmeg on crème brûlée. The palate has lemon, orange, pear, apple, and grassiness, with the IPA notes adding that snap of citrus bitterness to end the proceedings.

n: Whiskey Del Bac Frontera Spanish Sherry Cask Finished, 47.5%
t: Up front this presents a bouquet of peanut shells, pecan pie, and fruit snacks, all backed by waxy fruits and a slightly sharp hint of alcohol. The
f: Up front this presents a bouquet of peanut shells, pecan pie, and fruit snacks, all backed by waxy fruits and a slightly sharp hint of alcohol. The palate smooths out with blackberries, blueberries, and strawberry jam. Nestled beneath the fruitiness is dark chocolate, baking spices, and a dash of pepper. The finish has good length and a bit of soapiness alongside baking chocolate and well-integrated oak.

t: Very tropical on the nose, with hints of mango, lychee, and pineapple, plus roasty notes of woodsmoke and chocolate. Crisp and dry on a palate of
f: Very tropical on the nose, with hints of mango, lychee, and pineapple, plus roasty notes of woodsmoke and chocolate. Crisp and dry on a palate of dried fruits—pineapple, orange peel, and melon. The mouthfeel is light and syrupy sweet. Lingering notes of woodsmoke keep things in check, but sweet flavors of lemon and lemon cake take the lead. Unusually sweet and fruity, but no less interesting for it. (36,000 bottles)

n: Proof and Wood 7 year old Crossborder Jackpot, 53.5%
t: The nose is ripe with lemon peel and strong citrus. It turns sweeter the longer you stick with it, veering toward orange marmalade, lemonade, and a
f: The nose is ripe with lemon peel and strong citrus. It turns sweeter the longer you stick with it, veering toward orange marmalade, lemonade, and a bit of wood spice. That lemon follows through to the palate, where it's joined by a fiery burst of white pepper, vanilla extract, and tangy fruit. The finish is smooth and it lingers on, leaving the lemons behind in favor of vanilla. (4,836 bottles)

n: Middle West Spirits 6 year old Sherry Cask Finished, 48.62%
t: All sorts of berries flood the nose. Dig a little deeper, and there's strawberry tart, blueberry coulis, vanilla frosting, and cinnamon stick. A wave
f: All sorts of berries flood the nose. Dig a little deeper, and there's strawberry tart, blueberry coulis, vanilla frosting, and cinnamon stick. A wave of hot spice greets the palate, but the berries aren't gone for long; blueberry cobbler and strawberry ice cream intermingle with dark-roast coffee and cream. On the finish, there's chile chocolate that is mouthwatering and leaves you keen for more.

n: Barrell Cask Strength Blend of Straights (Batch 033), 58.3%
t: Sugary sweetness abounds on the nose; notes of cherry cordials, sugar cookie, vanilla frosting, and strawberry shortcake, plus dried herbs and
f: Sugary sweetness abounds on the nose; notes of cherry cordials, sugar cookie, vanilla frosting, and strawberry shortcake, plus dried herbs and green-tea ice cream. A velvety palate brings a wallop of heat and wood. Water tames both, bringing out peanut brittle, honey bun, dark chocolate, and camp coffee. Salted caramel highlights a lengthy finish. The heat makes this a bit jagged at times, though the texture is alluring. (33,000 bottles)

t: While rye whiskeys tend to lean into spicier notes, Gunpowder offers a sweet, charming take on the style. The nose is tropical and citrusy, with
f: While rye whiskeys tend to lean into spicier notes, Gunpowder offers a sweet, charming take on the style. The nose is tropical and citrusy, with dried pineapple, ripe mango, and sweet lime. There's orange soda, chocolate-orange, and new oak, too. The palate follows the nose, turning the sweetness up, with a rich mouthfeel. The finish introduces a bit of rye spice without stepping away from its sweet core.

n: Iron Fish Maple Syrup Barrel Finished, 43%
t: There is light fruitiness on the nose in the form of melon candy, apple, pear slices in syrup, and blueberry pie, alongside some new leather and
f: There is light fruitiness on the nose in the form of melon candy, apple, pear slices in syrup, and blueberry pie, alongside some new leather and chocolate-covered graham crackers. The palate is likewise syrupy, with notes of sweet mint and herbs, blackberry tart, and with water added, the woodiness of an antiques shop. A mid-length to short finish brings shortbread cookies, vanilla cream, and cider vinegar.

t: Chocolate comes forth on the nose: chocolate pudding, chocolate babka, hot fudge, chocolate-covered almonds, and chocolate Ovaltine. Delightfully,
f: Chocolate comes forth on the nose: chocolate pudding, chocolate babka, hot fudge, chocolate-covered almonds, and chocolate Ovaltine. Delightfully, those rich chocolaty flavors shine through to the palate, though they're now supplemented by red fruit. The heat on this one is incredible, so add water (and even then, the fire will remain) for a less spicy affair. The spicy, chocolate-fueled finish ties this up in the neatest of bows. (3,571 bottles)

t: On the nose this is light but delivers a broad bouquet: Sweet corn, lemon peel, and lime all rest on a backbone of wood sugar and barrel char. The
f: On the nose this is light but delivers a broad bouquet: Sweet corn, lemon peel, and lime all rest on a backbone of wood sugar and barrel char. The palate is like a fruit basket: cherries, candied orange, and pears, but more so a fruit snack quality pervades. The aroma and flavor of new oak holds this whiskey back a bit, and the finish borders on bitter.

t: Dry peppery spice and ample woody notes at the onset, with peppermint aromas building against a background of nuttiness, waxy leaves, and herbal
f: Dry peppery spice and ample woody notes at the onset, with peppermint aromas building against a background of nuttiness, waxy leaves, and herbal notes. Licorice, orange peel, and ground pepper are overcome by a deluge of clove, bitter herbs, and woodiness, then the creamy mouthfeel erupts amid notes of menthol, clove, and unsweetened chocolate. This is the choice for the accustomed single pot still drinker who prefers Powers to Redbreast.

n: Frey Ranch Barrel Strength Distiller’s Reserve Single Barrel (No. 260), 68.73%
t: Powerful and big on the nose, with baked chocolate brownies, plum pudding, cooked prunes, and woodsmoke. Water brings out spice notes of nutmeg,
f: Powerful and big on the nose, with baked chocolate brownies, plum pudding, cooked prunes, and woodsmoke. Water brings out spice notes of nutmeg, ginger, and vanilla. The palate is spicy, with blackberry tart, chocolate, blueberry pie, barrel char, and more vanilla. The finish is the best part, with balanced char, lots of deep chocolate, and some dark fruit. It's a hot one, but this is a very well-made whiskey.

n: Balcones Big Baby Bottled in Bond Tequila Cask Finished Corn Whiskey (Batch BB BiB 22-1), 50%
t: The nose is pungent, with overripe fruits, raisins, figs, apples, and apricots with a heavy pour of pepper. Water brings out a honeyed sweetness with
f: The nose is pungent, with overripe fruits, raisins, figs, apples, and apricots with a heavy pour of pepper. Water brings out a honeyed sweetness with notes of herbal cough drops. The palate leads with green veggies and black pepper. There's chocolate and instant coffee, too, but from palate to finish, this whiskey is predominantly peppery.

t: A blend of 15 and 16 year old bourbons. There is a lovely berry note on the nose, alongside milk chocolate, orange peel, leather, lilacs, spicy oak,
f: A blend of 15 and 16 year old bourbons. There is a lovely berry note on the nose, alongside milk chocolate, orange peel, leather, lilacs, spicy oak, and lemon icing. A lively palate brings cinnamon stick, buttered popcorn, snickerdoodle cookie, and peppery spice. The finish is long but thin, with lots of salinity. There's nice composition here and a balanced sweetness throughout, with spiced and earthy undertones.

n: Litchfield Distillery 5 year old Double Barreled, 45%
t: Herbal and citrus-forward aromas in the glass, reminiscent of Moroccan mint lemonade and lemon poppyseed muffins, plus baking spices and young oak.
f: Herbal and citrus-forward aromas in the glass, reminiscent of Moroccan mint lemonade and lemon poppyseed muffins, plus baking spices and young oak. While slightly woody, citrus and mint sing through. The palate is more subdued with lemon candies and strawberry soda enveloped in richer flavors of toffee and nougat. This wraps up like an Andes mint, with a long, dry finish.

t: The Irish-American whiskey trend works both ways. This golden dram serves up oak spices and lashings of creamy vanilla at 101 proof, with aromas of
f: The Irish-American whiskey trend works both ways. This golden dram serves up oak spices and lashings of creamy vanilla at 101 proof, with aromas of butter biscuits, sliced almond, and creamed coconut. Brown sugar, red fruits, and cherry lozenges on first sip, then cinder toffee, Milky Way, forest honey, and warm apple pie, ratcheting up lush vanilla, oakiness, and sweet concentrated fruitiness to finish. Water adds extra creaminess, if that's possible.  No. 2 in Top 20 2022.

n: New Riff 6 year old Sherry Finished, 56.35%
t: This malted rye is unabashedly dessert-like, drumming up candied pecans, shortbread cookies, maple syrup, Frosted Flakes, prunes, wood spice, and a
f: This malted rye is unabashedly dessert-like, drumming up candied pecans, shortbread cookies, maple syrup, Frosted Flakes, prunes, wood spice, and a sprinkle of cinnamon. That cinnamon spice is more of a contender on the palate, as Big Red gum and Red Hots take over before giving way to chocolate and dried fruit, an indicator of the port cask influence (if you didn't discern that from the deep amber color alone). A fiery finish takes this one home.

t: Dry notes of woodpile and plain Cheerios tee up the nose. It presents earthy and musty notes, with a zing of lemon zest and torched orange peel. The
f: Dry notes of woodpile and plain Cheerios tee up the nose. It presents earthy and musty notes, with a zing of lemon zest and torched orange peel. The palate is surprisingly gentle given the somewhat divisive nose, with citrus, dark-roast espresso, and semi-sweet chocolate playing well together. This certainly makes for a compelling journey. (24,000 bottles)

t: Inspired by winemakers, Talnua introduced charred virgin oak staves into the bourbon barrels for the duration of maturation: This is new territory
f: Inspired by winemakers, Talnua introduced charred virgin oak staves into the bourbon barrels for the duration of maturation: This is new territory for single pot still whiskey. The nose has vanilla ice cream, floral notes, fudge, candied peel, lemon zest, and dry wood spices. A fruity, sweet, easy sipper with apple, pear, vanilla, honey, cinnamon toffee, and creamy malt. The spicy finish offers vanilla pod, mouth-coating oils, and charred oak. (Colorado only)

t: Grandiose name for a perfectly acceptable but ultimately tame and straight-ahead Irish whiskey. There are hints of pot still oiliness, and the
f: Grandiose name for a perfectly acceptable but ultimately tame and straight-ahead Irish whiskey. There are hints of pot still oiliness, and the expected green fruits are in place. But the only new trick on offer here is the fact that it is less sweet and cloying than its brand siblings, the apples are like baked apples filled with mincemeat, with nutmeg and cinnamon in the mix. Frustrating, in that it hints at greatness but doesn't follow through.

n: Highwood 25 year old Calgary Stampede Centennial, 40%
t: A few years ago, Alberta's Highwood distillers purchased all the remaining stock from Potter's whisky brokerage just over the Rocky Mountains in
f: A few years ago, Alberta's Highwood distillers purchased all the remaining stock from Potter's whisky brokerage just over the Rocky Mountains in Kelowna. With it, Highwood skillfully created a sumptuous, limited-edition bottling that is as sweet, smooth, and creamy as French vanilla ice cream, and richer in fresh clean wood than a carpentry shop. Dried cloves and red cedar balance real maple syrup and butterscotch which, in turn, dissolve into sweet white grapefruit. (Alberta only) C$52

t: Well, what have we here? A blend of 50% malt and 50% grain (a very high malt content for a blend), and bottled at 50%, too! The whisky was blended
f: Well, what have we here? A blend of 50% malt and 50% grain (a very high malt content for a blend), and bottled at 50%, too! The whisky was blended first (very unusual), before being aged in sherry casks for its entire life. Antique amber/chestnut color. Full sherry impact, but never cloying -- the higher alcohol level and grain whisky cut through the sherry and add balance and drinkability. This is a fruity-confection delight, with raisin chutney, fig cake, orange almond scone, and chocolate-covered cherry. Add to the mix richly textured toffee, old oak, polished leather, and a cinnamon-spiced tobacco finish. A rare treat! A great old blend that malt drinkers will embrace.

n: Murray McDavid Mission IV (distilled at Clynelish), 1976 Vintage, 46%
t: Thick in texture and palate-coating. Ripe peaches and bananas, orange chocolate, English toffee, and a hint of damp oak on the nose. I can also
f: Thick in texture and palate-coating. Ripe peaches and bananas, orange chocolate, English toffee, and a hint of damp oak on the nose. I can also detect brine, seaweed, peat smoke, and spice, but it’s a little clumsy. Same story on the palate. Not a bad whisky, but I expect more from Clynelish.

t: Style: Speyside single malt scotch Color: Deep gold Aroma: Mature. Plenty of oak, but it’s clean. Coconut and citrus fruit. Background spices.
f: Style: Speyside single malt scotch Color: Deep gold Aroma: Mature. Plenty of oak, but it’s clean. Coconut and citrus fruit. Background spices. Palate: Lovely balance and restrained woodiness for such an old whisky-the wood really doesn’t emerge until the end. Citrus and coconut up front wrapped in a blanket of malt, becoming dry and spicy, but not excessively so. Delicate, lingering oak finish.

n: Gordon & MacPhail (distilled at Caol Ila), cask #00/3454, 15 year old, 1991 vintage, 46%
t: One of a series of single cask, wine-finished Caol Ilas. This one is finished in a claret (Bordeaux) wine cask. The claret adds some bright red fruit
f: One of a series of single cask, wine-finished Caol Ilas. This one is finished in a claret (Bordeaux) wine cask. The claret adds some bright red fruit notes (raspberry, red currant) and red licorice to accompany the smoke, brine, olive, and vanilla-laced malt. I have tasted some claret/Bordeaux wood-finished whiskies where the wine was too dominant, but this one achieves a nice balance.
